generations.description: The F5 generation refined the A5 with a lighter, stiffer structure. The RS5 switched to a twin-turbo 2.9 V6 — faster but more controversial than the outgoing V8. The RS5 Sportback particularly stands out as a practical everyday performance car.

generations.name: A6 C4 (1994–1997)
generations.description: The C4 was the first to wear the A6 name, replacing the 100. The S6 Plus — with a 326hp 4.2 V8 from the RS2 — was produced in tiny numbers and is now a genuine rarity sought by Audi collectors.

generations.name: A6 C5 (1997–2005)
generations.description: The C5 introduced the original RS6 — a 450hp twin-turbo V8 monster that shocked the executive saloon world. The RS6 Avant is particularly sought after and was not officially exported to some markets, making low-mileage examples increasingly rare.

generations.name: A6 C6 (2004–2011)
generations.engine_options: 2.0 TFSI,2.4,3.2 FSI,4.2 FSI,2.0 TDI,3.0 TDI,S6 5.2 V10,RS6 5.0 V10 Biturbo
generations.description: The C6 RS6 featured a spectacular 5.0 V10 Biturbo producing 580hp — the same block as the Lamborghini Gallardo. One of the most dramatic executive cars ever built, it remains a standout collector piece among Audi enthusiasts.

generations.name: A6 C7 (2011–2018)
generations.engine_options: 1.8 TFSI,2.0 TFSI,3.0 TFSI,2.0 TDI,3.0 TDI,S6 4.0 TFSI V8,RS6 4.0 TFSI V8 Biturbo
generations.description: The C7 RS6 Avant became a cultural phenomenon — a family estate with 560hp that could embarrass supercars. Celebrity ownership and viral video exposure turned it into one of the most desirable Audis of the modern era.

generations.name: A6 C8 (2018–present)
generations.engine_options: 2.0 TFSI,3.0 TFSI,2.0 TDI,3.0 TDI,S6 3.0 TDI,RS6 4.0 TFSI V8 Biturbo
generations.description: The C8 RS6 Avant arrived with 600hp, mild hybrid technology and more aggressive styling than ever before. Available in the US for the first time in Avant form, it immediately became Audi's halo performance wagon globally.

generations.name: A6 Allroad C5 (2000–2006)
generations.description: The original Allroad pioneered the concept of a raised all-wheel-drive estate before crossovers dominated. Pneumatic suspension was standard, offering variable ride height. The 2.7 Biturbo variant is the most desirable.

generations.name: A6 Allroad C7 (2012–2018)
generations.description: The C7 Allroad returned after a gap and refined the formula with more discreet styling and improved air suspension. A practical alternative to an SUV with genuine road and light off-road ability.

generations.name: A6 Allroad C8 (2019–present)
generations.engine_options: 45 TFSI quattro,55 TFSI quattro,40 TDI quattro,50 TDI quattro
generations.description: The C8 Allroad is the most polished version yet, blending premium comfort with genuine versatility. Air suspension and quattro all-wheel drive make it one of the most capable family estates on sale.

generations.name: A7 4G (2010–2018)
generations.engine_options: 2.0 TFSI,3.0 TFSI,3.0 TDI,4.0 TFSI,S7 4.0 TFSI V8,RS7 4.0 TFSI V8 Biturbo
generations.description: The A7 Sportback's fastback silhouette was immediately acclaimed as one of Audi's finest designs. The RS7 — with 560hp twin-turbo V8 and a four-door fastback body — combined supercar pace with daily usability in a way few cars could match.

generations.name: A7 4K (2018–present)
generations.engine_options: 2.0 TFSI,3.0 TFSI,3.0 TDI,55 TFSI,S7 3.0 TDI,RS7 4.0 TFSI V8 Biturbo
generations.description: The second generation A7 added mild hybrid technology and an even more dramatic interior. The RS7 Performance with 630hp is among the fastest Audis ever offered to the public.

generations.name: A8 D2 (1994–2002)
generations.description: The D2 A8 was a landmark car — the first volume production aluminium space-frame saloon, revolutionary for its time. The S8 with 360hp V8 was a genuine Q-car, and the W12 flagship remains an imposing grand tourer.

generations.name: A8 D3 (2002–2010)
generations.description: The D3 S8 featured a 450hp naturally aspirated 5.2 V10 from the Lamborghini Gallardo — making it a rare Q-car of the highest order. Low mileage examples are becoming genuinely collectible.

generations.name: A8 D4 (2009–2017)
generations.engine_options: 3.0 TFSI,4.0 TFSI,4.2 TDI,6.3 W12,S8 4.0 TFSI V8 Biturbo
generations.description: The D4 S8 with 520hp twin-turbo V8 is arguably the definitive Audi super-saloon. Deceptively discreet on the outside, devastating on the road. Values have stabilised making this an accessible performance bargain.

generations.name: A8 D5 (2017–present)
generations.engine_options: 3.0 TFSI,4.0 TFSI,6.0 W12,S8 4.0 TFSI V8 Biturbo
generations.description: The D5 A8 pushes technology furthest with mild hybrid systems, active suspension, and semi-autonomous driving aids. The S8 with 571hp remains a formidable super-saloon, while the W12 flagship is the last of a dying breed.

generations.name: Q2 GA (2016–present)
generations.engine_options: 1.0 TFSI,1.4 TFSI,1.5 TFSI,2.0 TFSI,1.6 TDI,2.0 TDI,SQ2 2.0 TFSI quattro
generations.description: The Q2 is Audi's entry-level crossover, distinguished by its bold C-pillar contrast panel. The SQ2 with 300hp quattro all-wheel drive is the performance variant and the one most likely to develop a collector following as a characterful small fast SUV.

generations.name: Q3 8U (2011–2018)
generations.description: The first Q3 brought Audi's premium compact SUV formula to a smaller footprint. The RSQ3 with the five-cylinder 2.5 TFSI — shared with the RS3 — is the enthusiast target, delivering a unique soundtrack and 310hp in a practical package.

generations.name: Q3 F3 (2018–present)
generations.engine_options: 1.5 TFSI,2.0 TFSI,1.5 TDI,2.0 TDI,RSQ3 2.5 TFSI quattro,RSQ3 Sportback
generations.description: The second generation Q3 grew in size and added the Sportback body. The RSQ3 retained the beloved five-cylinder engine now producing 400hp, making it one of the most entertaining compact SUVs available. The Sportback RSQ3 in particular has attracted strong collector interest.

generations.name: Q4 e-tron (2021–present)
generations.engine_options: 40 e-tron,45 e-tron,50 e-tron quattro,Q4 Sportback e-tron
generations.description: The Q4 e-tron is Audi's first fully electric SUV on the VW Group MEB platform. Offered as standard SUV and Sportback, it represents the accessible entry point to Audi's electric lineup. The 50 quattro all-wheel-drive variant is the performance choice.

generations.name: Q5 8R (2008–2017)
generations.engine_options: 2.0 TFSI,2.0 TDI,3.0 TDI,3.2 FSI,SQ5 3.0 TFSI supercharged,SQ5 TDI
generations.description: The first Q5 established Audi's mid-size SUV benchmark. The SQ5 3.0 TFSI supercharged — later replaced by a TDI variant in some markets — is the driver's choice, offering genuine performance with everyday versatility.

generations.name: Q5 FY (2016–present)
generations.engine_options: 2.0 TFSI,3.0 TFSI,2.0 TDI,3.0 TDI,SQ5 3.0 TFSI,SQ5 TDI,RSQ5
generations.description: The second generation Q5 added the Sportback body style and brought plug-in hybrid options. The SQ5 remains the driver's choice, and the recently introduced RSQ5 with 500hp twin-turbo V6 has immediately established itself as the performance flagship.

generations.name: Q7 4L (2005–2015)
generations.engine_options: 3.0 TFSI,3.6 FSI,4.2 FSI,3.0 TDI,4.2 TDI,6.0 V12 TDI,SQ7
generations.description: The original Q7 was Audi's first full-size SUV, establishing the three-row formula. The V12 TDI — producing 500hp and a colossal 1,000Nm of torque from a diesel — is one of the most extraordinary engines ever fitted to an SUV and is now a genuine collector piece.

generations.name: Q7 4M (2015–present)
generations.engine_options: 2.0 TFSI,3.0 TFSI,3.0 TDI,SQ7 4.0 TDI,SQ7 TFSI,e-tron PHEV
generations.description: The 4M Q7 shed considerable weight through aluminium construction and added air suspension. The SQ7 TDI — with an electric compressor for near-zero turbo lag — was a technical tour de force and demonstrated diesel performance at its finest before electrification took hold.

generations.name: Q8 4M (2018–present)
generations.engine_options: 3.0 TFSI,3.0 TDI,55 TFSI,SQ8 4.0 TFSI V8,RSQ8 4.0 TFSI V8 Biturbo
generations.description: The Q8 is Audi's flagship SUV coupe, combining the practicality of a full-size SUV with fastback styling. The RSQ8 with 600hp twin-turbo V8 set Nürburgring SUV records on launch and remains one of the fastest SUVs on sale. Low-mileage RSQ8 examples are already appreciating.

generations.name: e-tron (2018–2023)
generations.description: The original e-tron was Audi's first fully electric production car — a full-size SUV with dual motors and quattro electric all-wheel drive. The S e-tron with 503hp and launch control established that electric performance was serious. First editions and S variants are the early collector targets.

generations.name: Q8 e-tron (2023–present)
generations.description: Renamed Q8 e-tron for its mid-cycle update, this generation brought meaningfully improved range, faster charging and refined driving dynamics. The SQ8 e-tron with 503hp remains the performance flagship of Audi's electric SUV lineup.

generations.name: e-tron GT (2021–present)
generations.engine_options: e-tron GT quattro,RS e-tron GT,RS e-tron GT Performance
generations.description: The e-tron GT is arguably Audi's most significant electric car — a four-door gran turismo sharing its J1 platform with the Porsche Taycan. The RS e-tron GT with 646hp is genuinely rapid and its Pininfarina-influenced styling has been near-universally praised. First-generation examples — especially the launch Edition One — are already tracking as collectibles.

generations.name: Q6 e-tron (2024–present)
generations.description: The Q6 e-tron debuts on the Premium Platform Electric (PPE) architecture co-developed with Porsche. It represents a step change in Audi's EV capability — 800V charging, faster software, and sharper dynamics. The SQ6 with 489hp is the performance variant and one of the most capable electric mid-size SUVs yet produced.

generations.name: A6 e-tron (2024–present)
generations.description: The A6 e-tron brings the PPE electric platform to a saloon and Avant body — significant because it marks the first time Audi has offered a fully electric estate. The S6 e-tron Avant in particular has attracted attention as a Tesla Model S Shooting Brake alternative with proper Audi build quality.

generations.name: Scout 80 (1961–1965)
generations.description: The original Scout 80 essentially invented the compact recreational 4x4 category, predating the Ford Bronco and Chevrolet Blazer by years. Its simple, rugged design and removable top made it an instant hit with outdoor enthusiasts. Early examples with the original 4-cylinder are now serious collector pieces.

generations.name: Scout 800 (1965–1971)
generations.description: The 800 brought a longer wheelbase, more power options including a V8, and better refinement to the Scout formula. The 800A and 800B variants refined it further. These are the most versatile of the early Scouts — powerful enough for serious off-road use, simple enough to restore.

generations.name: Scout II (1971–1980)
generations.description: The Scout II is the definitive International Harvester collector vehicle. A longer, more capable platform offered with a wide range of engines including the legendary 345 and 392 V8s. The Rallye trim, Ssport package, and Terra pickup variants are particularly sought after. Values have risen sharply as the overlanding and vintage 4x4 movements have grown.

generations.name: Travelall (1953–1975)
generations.description: The Travelall was International Harvester's answer to the Chevrolet Suburban — a full-size four-door wagon offered in both two and four-wheel drive long before the SUV was a recognised segment. It predated the Ford Bronco and Blazer concept by a decade. Low survival rates and growing collector recognition make original examples increasingly valuable.

generations.name: IH Pickup C/D/R-Series (1950–1975)
generations.description: International Harvester pickups competed directly with Ford and Chevrolet through the postwar decades. The C, D, and R series trucks are known for their durability and distinctive styling. The 345 and 392 V8 options make them genuine performers, and low-rider examples have a strong custom truck following alongside traditionalist collectors.

generations.name: Saab 92/93/96 (1950–1980)
generations.description: The Saab 96 and its predecessors established Saab's reputation for unconventional engineering and rally success. The two-stroke early cars are unique collector pieces, while the later V4 models are more practical. Erik Carlsson's works rally victories cemented the 96's motorsport legend. Monte Carlo Rally winners are among the most valuable.

generations.name: Saab 99 (1968–1984)
generations.description: The Saab 99 Turbo of 1977 was a landmark car — one of the first turbocharged production cars in the world and a genuine performance pioneer. The Turbo and Turbo Combi Coupe variants transformed Saab's image and are the collector targets today. The EMS (Electronic Management System) variants are also sought after.

generations.name: Saab 900 Classic (1978–1994)
generations.description: The original 900 is the definitive Saab — quirky, practical, turbocharged and deeply characterful. The Turbo 16 and SPG (Special Performance Group) are the performance highlights. The Convertible — one of few true four-seat cabriolets of its era — has become particularly collectible. The Aero badge on later cars denotes the full-specification Turbo.

generations.name: Saab 900 NG (1994–1998)
generations.description: The New Generation 900 shared its platform with Opel/Vauxhall following GM's acquisition of Saab. More conventional than its predecessor but still distinctive. The Aero Turbo and Convertible remain the most desirable variants. Often overshadowed by the classic 900 but appreciated for its refinement.

generations.name: Saab 9000 (1984–1998)
generations.description: The 9000 was Saab's flagship and remains the most performance-capable of the classic Saabs. The 9000 Aero with 225hp turbocharged 2.3 was genuinely rapid and handled well. The CD (saloon) and CS (hatchback) Aero variants are the collector targets. Low-mileage Aero examples have appreciated significantly.

generations.name: Saab 9-3 Gen 1 (1998–2002)
generations.description: The first 9-3 replaced the 900 NG and introduced the Viggen — a 230hp hot hatch with a unique front-wheel-drive torque management system. The Viggen is the standout collector car of this generation, controversial on launch but now appreciated as a genuinely characterful performance car.

generations.name: Saab 9-3 Gen 2 (2002–2011)
generations.description: The second generation 9-3 was Saab's most commercially successful car in years. The Aero with 2.8 V6 Turbo and the Hirsch-prepared variants are the performance highlights. The Cabriolet and SportCombi estate are the most distinctive body styles. Late production cars and Special Edition models are already developing collector interest as Saab's final years.

generations.name: Saab 9-5 Gen 1 (1997–2010)
generations.description: The 9-5 was Saab's executive saloon and estate, competing with BMW 5 Series and Mercedes E-Class. The Aero and Hirsch-tuned variants with 250hp+ turbocharged 2.3 are rapid and undervalued. The estate (SportCombi) is particularly practical and increasingly appreciated as a long-distance touring machine.

generations.name: Saab 9-5 Gen 2 (2010–2011)
generations.description: The second generation 9-5 arrived just as Saab's financial difficulties reached a crisis point. Production lasted barely a year before the company collapsed. The very low production numbers — particularly for the estate and V6 XWD variants — make these among the rarest modern Saabs. A legitimate future collectible purely on rarity.

generations.name: Amazon / 120 Series (1956–1970)
generations.description: The Amazon established Volvo's reputation for safety and durability. Its three-point seatbelt — standard from 1959 — was a world first. The 123GT sport variant with twin carburettors and bucket seats is the collector highlight, along with two-door saloon examples. Clean surviving examples command strong prices as pre-safety-regulation classics.

generations.name: Volvo 1800 (1961–1973)
generations.description: The Volvo 1800 is one of the most elegant Scandinavian cars ever built. The P1800 coupe gained fame as Roger Moore's car in The Saint television series. The 1800ES shooting brake estate — one of the first of its kind — is considered the rarest and most desirable variant. A genuine sports car that also happened to be a Volvo.

generations.name: 140 Series (1966–1974)
generations.description: The 140 series scaled up the Amazon formula into a larger family car while retaining the same engineering robustness. The 142 two-door coupe is the most stylish variant and the one that attracts collectors. The GT package added sport trim and twin carburettors. Remarkably rust-resistant examples still surface in Sweden and Norway.

generations.name: 240 Series (1974–1993)
generations.engine_options: 2.0L B20,2.1L B21,2.3L B23,2.3L B230,2.4L diesel,Turbo B21ET
generations.description: The Volvo 240 is one of the longest-running and most successful car models ever built. Its boxy proportions became iconic and its reputation for longevity is unmatched — 300,000-mile examples are not rare. The Turbo and the GLT sport variants are the performance highlights. The estate is the most beloved body style and has a cult following worldwide.

generations.name: 260 Series (1974–1982)
generations.description: The 260 series brought a jointly-developed Peugeot-Renault-Volvo V6 to the Volvo lineup. The 262C Bertone coupe is the standout variant — a luxury two-door with a lower roofline designed by Bertone that brought genuine European style to Volvo's range. Low survival rates make good 262C examples increasingly rare.

generations.name: Volvo 480 (1986–1995)
generations.description: The 480 was Volvo's unexpected sports car — a front-wheel-drive coupe with pop-up headlights and a wedge silhouette that bore no resemblance to anything else in the Volvo range. Developed in the Netherlands, it was a commercial underperformer but is now appreciated as a genuinely stylish oddity. The Turbo is the performance variant and the ES convertible the rarest.

generations.engine_options: 2.3L B230,2.3L Turbo B230ET,2.8L PRV V6,2.4L diesel
generations.description: The 700 series replaced the 240 at the top of Volvo's range with a more modern shape that still kept the boxy Volvo character. The 740 Turbo and 760 Turbo are the performance highlights. The 760 GLE with the PRV V6 was the flagship. Estates in good condition are becoming difficult to find and are appreciating accordingly.

generations.name: 850 / 850 T-5R / 850 R (1991–1997)
generations.description: The 850 was a revelation — a front-wheel-drive Volvo that was genuinely fast and handled well. The T-5R and 850R variants with 240hp turbocharged five-cylinder competed in the British Touring Car Championship, giving Volvo an unexpected motorsport image. The estate racing car remains one of the most famous competition wagons ever built.

generations.name: V70 R / S70 R (1997–2000)
generations.description: The V70 R brought all-wheel drive to the performance Volvo estate formula, producing one of the finest performance wagons of the 1990s. 250hp, AWD, and the practicality of a large estate made it a cult favourite. Clean low-mileage examples are increasingly rare and command strong collector premiums.

generations.name: Volvo C30 (2006–2013)
generations.description: The C30 was Volvo's first sports hatchback and a genuine design statement — its glassback rear end referenced the P1800ES shooting brake. The T5 with 230hp is the hot hatch variant and a future collectible. The electric C30 EV was a limited production pioneer of Volvo's electrification strategy.

generation_summaries.description: The Ferrari 250 GTO is the most valuable road-racing car ever made. Built to compete in GT racing, just 39 were produced. Every example is individually documented and authenticated.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Series I, Series II, Series III, Series I, Series II, Series III

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Series I, Series II, Series III

generation_summaries.description: The 250 GT Lusso is the grand touring companion to the GTO, penned by Pininfarina. Long-nosed and beautiful, it was Steve McQueen's personal car and represents the apex of 1960s Ferrari road car design.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The 275 GTB introduced independent rear suspension to Ferrari road cars. The four-cam GTB/4 variant is the most coveted, while the NART Spider is among the rarest open Ferraris ever built.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTB, GTB/4, GTS NART Spider, GTB, GTB/4, GTS, GTB/4 NART Spider, GTB/C

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GTB, GTB/4, GTS NART Spider, GTS, GTB/4 NART Spider, GTB/C

generation_summaries.engine_options: 3.0 L Colombo V8,2.9 L V8 Turbo
generation_summaries.description: The Ferrari 308 brought the mid-engine V8 formula to a wider audience. Penned by Pininfarina, it remains one of the most recognisable shapes in automotive history. QV examples with the four-valve head are the pick of the range.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTB, GTS, GTBi/GTSi, GTB QV, GTS QV

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GTB, GTS, GTBi/GTSi, GTB QV, GTS QV

generation_summaries.description: The 328 refined the 308 formula with a larger 3.2-litre engine and restyled bodywork. The last of the classic Pininfarina mid-engine V8 line before the 348, it is increasingly sought after as a usable classic.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTB, GTS

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GTB, GTS

generation_summaries.description: The Testarossa's straked side intakes made it the defining supercar silhouette of the 1980s. A genuine 180mph car, it was Ferrari's flagship for over a decade. Single-mirror early cars command significant premiums.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Testarossa, 512 TR, F512 M, Testarossa, 512 TR, F512 M

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Testarossa, 512 TR, F512 M

generation_summaries.description: Built to celebrate Ferrari's 40th anniversary, the F40 was the last car Enzo personally approved. With no driver aids, no carpets, and raw twin-turbo power, it remains the purest supercar of its era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, LM, GTE, F40, F40 LM, F40 Competizione

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, LM, GTE, F40, F40 LM, F40 Competizione

generation_summaries.description: The F355 revived Ferrari's fortunes with a spectacular 375bhp five-valve-per-cylinder V8 and sublime handling. The Spider with manual gearbox is the collector's choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Berlinetta, GTS, Spider, Challenge

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Berlinetta, GTS, Spider, Challenge

generation_summaries.description: The Dino was Ferrari's first mid-engine road car. Never badged as a Ferrari during production, it is now fully accepted into the canon. The GTS Targa is increasingly preferred for open-air driving.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 206 GT, 246 GT, 246 GTS, M series, E series, L series

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 206 GT, 246 GT, 246 GTS, M series, E series, L series

generation_summaries.description: The Daytona was the last front-engined Ferrari supercar before the mid-engine era. Named unofficially after Ferrari's 1-2-3 finish at the 1967 Daytona 24 Hours, the Spider version is extraordinarily rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTB/4, GTS/4 Spider, Competizione, Daytona, Daytona Spider, Competizione, Spyder

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GTB/4, GTS/4 Spider, Competizione, Daytona, Daytona Spider, Spyder

generation_summaries.description: The Berlinetta Boxer was Ferrari's first mid-engine 12-cylinder road car. Visually dramatic and mechanically complex, later fuel-injected 512 BBi examples are more reliable but the carburetted 512 BB is the purist's choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 365 GT4 BB, 512 BB, 512 BBi

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 365 GT4 BB, 512 BB, 512 BBi

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.1 L Flat-4,1.3 L Flat-4,1.6 L Flat-4
generation_summaries.description: The 356 is where Porsche began. Built initially from Volkswagen components, it evolved into a sophisticated sports car. The Speedster is the most iconic body style; pre-A coupes are the most historically significant.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Pre-A, 356 A, 356 B, 356 C, Speedster, Carrera GS, Abarth Carrera, Pre-A Coupe

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.6 L Flat-4,1.6 L Carrera GS,2.0 L Carrera 2
generation_summaries.description: The 356 B and C represent the mature expression of the original Porsche formula. The Carrera 2 with its twin-cam four-cylinder is the ultimate performance variant. The final C model with Porsche's first disc brakes was the most refined 356 and sold in the smallest numbers.
generation_summaries.key_variants: B Coupe, B Cabriolet, B Roadster, B Super 90, C Coupe, C Cabriolet, Carrera 2, B Coupe

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Pre-A, 356 A, 356 B, 356 C, Speedster, Carrera GS, Abarth Carrera, Pre-A Coupe, Pre-A Cabriolet, A Coupe

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L Flat-6,2.2 L Flat-6,2.4 L Flat-6
generation_summaries.description: The original long-hood 911 is the most historically significant sports car of the postwar era. Early 2.0-litre S models and the 1973 Carrera RS 2.7 represent the pinnacle. Rust and accident history are the primary concerns.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 911 S, 911 E, 911 T, Carrera RS 2.7, 911 ST

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L Flat-6,2.2 L Flat-6,2.4 L Flat-6
generation_summaries.description: The F-series 911 with the 2.4 S is the purest driving expression of the early air-cooled car -- light, responsive, and with throttle-steerable handling that rewards the skilled driver. The 1973 RS Touring and Lightweight are the peak of the generation.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 911 S, 911 E, 911 T, 2.4 S, 2.4 E, 911 RS, RS Touring, RS Lightweight

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.7 L Flat-6,3.0 L Flat-6,2.7 RS,3.0 RSR
generation_summaries.description: The G-series introduced the impact bumpers but also the 2.7 RS -- arguably the most important 911 road car ever made. With just 1,580 built for homologation, the lightweight Touring and Sport variants are among the most valuable 911s at auction.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Carrera, Carrera S, 2.7 RS, 3.0 RS, 930 Turbo, Carrera Targa

generation_summaries.description: The 930 Turbo was the fastest production car in the world when launched and earned a fearsome reputation. The early 3.0 cars are the most dramatic; the 3.3 is more manageable. Widowmaker is the nickname — earned.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 3.0 Turbo, 3.3 Turbo, Turbo SE, Slant Nose

generation_summaries.description: The 911 SC is the most overlooked classic 911. Reliable, sorted, and driving beautifully — it benefits from decades of development without the premiums of the Carrera 3.2. The Cabriolet of 1983 was the first open 911 since the 356. An undervalued entry point.
generation_summaries.key_variants: SC, SC Cabriolet, Super Carrera

generation_summaries.description: The 3.2 Carrera was the final evolution of the original 911 before the 964. Bosch Motronic fuel injection, G50 gearbox from 1987, and the best balance of old-school character with modern reliability. Club Sport and Speedster variants are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Carrera, Carrera Cabriolet, Carrera Targa, Club Sport, Speedster, M491 Turbo-Look

generation_summaries.description: The 964 was the first major redesign of the 911 since 1963, yet retained the air-cooled soul purists demand. The RS is one of the most coveted road cars of the era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Carrera 2, Carrera 4, RS, Turbo 3.3, Turbo 3.6, RS America, Speedster

generation_summaries.description: The 993 was the last air-cooled 911 and is widely regarded as the finest. Its multi-link rear suspension transformed handling and the twin-turbo Turbo S is among the fastest cars of the decade.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Carrera, Carrera 4, Carrera RS, Turbo, Turbo S, GT2, Targa, Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The 993 GT2 is the most extreme road car Porsche made in the air-cooled era. Rear-wheel drive, twin-turbocharged, 430bhp, and stripped for racing homologation. Just 194 road cars were built. The ultimate air-cooled Porsche.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT2, GT2 Evo

generation_summaries.description: The 996 GT3 introduced the Metzger engine — a motorsport-derived unit shared with the GT1 racer. Despised initially for the water-cooled transition, the GT3 is now recognised as a superb driver's car. The RS variants are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT3, GT3 RS, GT3 Cup

generation_summaries.engine_options: 3.4 L Flat-6,3.6 L Flat-6 Turbo,3.6 L GT2,3.6 L GT3
generation_summaries.description: The 996 was the most controversial 911 -- water-cooled, with a shared front end with the Boxster. Values have bottomed and are recovering, making early GT3s and Turbos strong buys. The IMS bearing issue on non-GT cars is a known factor that buyers must address.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Carrera, Carrera 4, Carrera 4S, Turbo, GT3, GT3 RS, GT2, Targa

generation_summaries.engine_options: 3.6 L Flat-6,3.8 L Flat-6,3.6 L Turbo,3.8 L GT3,3.6 L GT2
generation_summaries.description: The 997 is widely considered the sweet spot of the modern 911 -- corrected styling, a return to the classic 911 face, and a naturally aspirated GT3 that many regard as the finest driver's car of its generation. Gen 1 GT3 RS 3.8 and Gen 2 GT3 RS 4.0 are the definitive collector variants.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Carrera, Carrera S, Carrera 4S, Turbo, Turbo S, GT3, GT3 RS, GT3 RS 4.0

generation_summaries.description: The 997 GT3 RS brought the GT3's motorsport DNA to its most extreme road expression. Wider body, coilover suspension, and the choice of 3.6 or 3.8-litre naturally aspirated flat-sixes. The GT3 RS 4.0 — last air-cooled-style Porsche engine — is the ultimate.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT3 RS 3.6, GT3 RS 3.8, GT3 RS 4.0

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Carrera 2, Carrera 4, RS, Turbo 3.3, Turbo 3.6, RS America, Speedster, 911 S, 911 E, 911 T

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.7 L Flat-4,2.0 L Flat-4,2.0 L Flat-6
generation_summaries.description: The mid-engine 914 was a joint Porsche-VW project and was derided on launch. Today the six-cylinder 914/6 is a legitimate collector car and even the four-cylinder cars have a dedicated following.

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.5 L I4,2.7 L I4,3.0 L I4 Turbo
generation_summaries.description: The 944 was Porsche's volume seller in the 1980s. The Turbo is the driver's pick; the S2 has the largest naturally aspirated four ever fitted to a production car. Turbos with full service history are increasingly collectible.

The 944 S2 with its 3.0-litre four is the most powerful normally-aspirated 944 and the most complete version of the model. The S2 Cabriolet is an increasingly desirable open car; very few were built and survivors in original condition are genuinely scarce.
generation_summaries.key_variants: S2 Coupe, S2 Cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 944, 944 S, 944 Turbo, 944 S2, 944 Turbo S, 944 S2 early, S2 Coupe, S2 Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The 959 was the most technically advanced road car of its era — sequential twin-turbos, all-wheel drive, adjustable suspension, and 450bhp. It previewed technology the industry took a decade to adopt.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Komfort, Sport

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Komfort, Sport

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.5 L Flat-6,2.7 L Flat-6,3.2 L Flat-6 S
generation_summaries.description: The 986 Boxster saved Porsche from bankruptcy and established mid-engine roadster credentials. The early 2.5 IMS bearing issue is the key concern; post-2000 cars with the upgraded bearing are more reliable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Boxster, Boxster S, Boxster, Boxster S, 986

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.7 L Flat-6,3.2 L S,3.4 L Spyder,3.4 L R
generation_summaries.description: The 987 Boxster corrected the 986's styling missteps and added the Spyder and R variants that have become genuine collector items. The Boxster Spyder with its manual folding top and 320 hp is the driver's choice; the RS60 Spyder tribute edition is a rare limited piece.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Boxster, Boxster S, Boxster Spyder, Boxster R, RS60 Spyder

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Boxster, Boxster S, 986, Boxster Spyder, Boxster R, RS60 Spyder

generation_summaries.description: The original Mustang created the pony car class overnight. Fastbacks and Boss variants are the collector targets. Shelbys occupy a category of their own.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT, Mach 1, Boss 302, Boss 429, Shelby GT350, Shelby GT500

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.3 L I4,2.8 L V6,5.0 L V8 Cobra II
generation_summaries.description: Long dismissed, the Mustang II is gaining collector respect, especially the Cobra II and King Cobra editions. The highest-optioned Ghia coupes in original condition are becoming a niche find.
generation_summaries.key_variants: V8, Ghia, Mach 1, Cobra II, King Cobra, Sprint

generation_summaries.engine_options: 5.0 L HO V8,2.3 L Turbo,5.8 L GT500
generation_summaries.description: The Fox-body Mustang GT and Cobra represent one of the great performance bargains of the 1980s and are maturing into collectibles. The 1993 SVT Cobra and 1993 Cobra R are the standout limited editions.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT, LX 5.0, Cobra, Cobra R, GT350, GT500, Special Service, Saleen

generation_summaries.engine_options: 4.6 L SOHC V8,4.6 L DOHC Cobra,5.4 L Terminator
generation_summaries.description: The 2003-04 SVT Cobra Terminator -- supercharged 4.6 producing a factory-conservative 390 hp -- has become a serious modern collector car.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT, Cobra, Cobra R, Mach 1, Bullitt, GT Premium, V6, SVT Cobra

generation_summaries.engine_options: 5.4 L Supercharged V8,5.8 L Supercharged V8
generation_summaries.description: The SVT Shelby GT500 returned the supercharged big-block formula to the Mustang for the first time since the 1960s. The 2013 upgrade to the 5.8-litre Trinity V8 produced 662bhp — briefly the most powerful production V8 in the world. Glass roof option unique to this generation.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT500, GT500 Convertible, Glass Roof, Super Snake

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GT, Mach 1, Boss 302, Boss 429, Shelby GT350, Shelby GT500, GT500, GT500 Convertible, Glass Roof, Super Snake

generation_summaries.description: Built to beat Ferrari at Le Mans, the GT40 succeeded with four consecutive overall victories 1966–1969. Road cars are among the most valuable American vehicles ever built. Continuation cars require careful authentication.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mk I, Mk II, Mk III Road Car, Mk IV

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Mk I, Mk II, Mk III Road Car, Mk IV

generation_summaries.description: The original two-seat Thunderbird was Ford's response to the Corvette. Its 1955–57 run is the most collectible — the addition of rear seats in 1958 marked the end of the sports car era. Porthole hardtops are especially desirable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Porthole Hardtop, base, hardtop, porthole hardtop, roadster

generation_summaries.description: The 1958-60 Square Bird traded the two-seater's purity for four seats and immediately became the best-selling convertible in America. The 1958 is the first-year square body; hardtop examples with the Continental kit are among the most photographed 1950s Fords.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Convertible, Hardtop, Continental Kit

generation_summaries.description: The 1961-63 Bullet Bird -- with its distinctive pointed nose and Sports Roadster option -- is the most elegant Thunderbird. The Sports Roadster with fiberglass tonneau covering the rear seats and wire wheels is a rare and exceptional open car.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Hardtop, Convertible, Sports Roadster, Landau

generation_summaries.description: The 1964-66 Thunderbird gained a longer body and the Landau roofline that would define personal luxury for a decade. The 1966 convertible in its final year of the body style is the most desirable of the trio.

generation_summaries.description: The C5 Z06 transformed the Corvette from a cruise missile into a proper track weapon. The LS6 engine, Bilstein shocks, and titanium exhaust produced a car that humiliated Ferraris at a fraction of the price. Fixed roof coupe only — no convertible Z06.

generation_summaries.description: The C6 ZR1 was the most powerful production Corvette ever made at launch — 638bhp from a supercharged LS9 hand-built at the Corvette engine plant. Carbon ceramic brakes, carbon hood, and a top speed of 205mph. Outran everything at its price point.
generation_summaries.key_variants: ZR1

generation_summaries.description: The 450SEL 6.9 was the fastest four-door car in the world when launched. Hydropneumatic self-levelling suspension and a 286bhp engine made it the S-Class benchmark. The drivers' car of choice for Saudi royalty and racing drivers.
The 500E was hand-assembled by Porsche — each car spent three days at Zuffenhausen. A 326bhp 5-litre V8 in a mid-size Mercedes, it remains the benchmark Q-car. Only 10,479 were built.

The 507 is one of the most beautiful cars of the 20th century. Designed by Albrecht von Goertz, only 252 were made. Elvis Presley owned two. BMW almost went bankrupt building it at a loss, leading to the company's near-sale.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Roadster

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Roadster

generation_summaries.description: The 2002 is the car that defined BMW's character — a compact, rear-drive coupe with an eager engine and sharp handling. It created the sports sedan segment. The tii with Kugelfischer fuel injection is the driver's pick; the Turbo the 1973 collector's piece. The Cabriolet by Baur is the rarest factory variant.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1600-2, 2002, 2002 tii, 2002 ti, Touring, Cabriolet Baur, 1600-2, 2002

generation_summaries.description: The 2002 Turbo was Europe's first turbocharged production car. Aggressive reverse-stencilled bodywork and a distinctive spoiler made it instantly recognisable. Only 1,672 were made and most have survived.

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 2002, 2002 ti, 2002 tii, 2002 Turbo, 1600-2, Touring, Cabriolet Baur, 2002A, 2002 Cabriolet, 2002 Touring

generation_summaries.description: The M1 is BMW's only true mid-engine supercar. Designed by Giugiaro and built with help from Lamborghini, it competed in the one-make Procar series. The road car is rarer than many exotics and increasingly sought after.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Procar, M1 road car, M1 Procar

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Procar, M1 road car, M1 Procar

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.3 L S14 I4,2.5 L S14 Evolution
generation_summaries.description: Built to homologate BMW for touring car racing, the E30 M3 is the purest driver's car BMW ever made. Sport Evolution examples are among the most coveted BMWs in existence.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Evo I, Evo II, Sport Evolution, M3 coupe, M3 convertible, M3 Sport Evolution, M3 Evo II

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Evo I, Evo II, Sport Evolution, M3 coupe, M3 convertible, M3 Sport Evolution, M3 Evo II, M3 DTM

generation_summaries.description: The E28 M5 was the world's fastest production sedan when launched. Hand-built by BMW Motorsport with the M1's engine in a discreet sedan body — the original Q-car. Only 2,241 were made.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, US Spec

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, US Spec

generation_summaries.description: The E46 M3 is widely regarded as the finest M car BMW has made. The naturally aspirated S54 engine to 8,000rpm and hydraulic steering define the experience. CSL and GTR variants are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Coupe, Cabriolet, CSL, GTR, Competition Package, M3 coupe, M3 convertible, M3 CSL

generation_summaries.description: The M3 GTR was built purely for American Le Mans Series homologation — BMW's rules required 10 road cars to race the V8-engined GTR. Each road car cost $250,000 and used a 4.0-litre V8 derived from the race car. One of the rarest and most extreme BMW road cars ever built.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTR Road Car

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Coupe, Cabriolet, CSL, GTR, Competition Package, M3 coupe, M3 convertible, M3 CSL, M3 Competition, GTR Road Car

generation_summaries.description: The Miura is widely considered the world's first supercar. Its transverse mid-mounted V12 and Bertone body set the template for every supercar that followed. SV is the definitive variant.
generation_summaries.key_variants: P400, P400 S, P400 SV, Jota, P400, P400 Roadster concept

generation_summaries.description: The Miura SV is the ultimate evolution of the original supercar formula -- more power, wider rear tyres, and separated oil sumps for the engine and gearbox. Of the 764 Miuras built, the SV is the most desirable; cars with the factory-optional Jota specification are extraordinary rarities.
generation_summaries.key_variants: P400 S, P400 SV, SV Jota

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: P400, P400 S, P400 SV, Jota, P400 Roadster concept, SV Jota

generation_summaries.description: The Countach defined the supercar poster era. Bertone's impossibly dramatic wedge shape made every other car look ordinary. The LP400 "periscopio" is the purist's car; LP5000 QV the fastest. Wings are optional aesthetics.
generation_summaries.key_variants: LP400, LP400 S, LP500 S, LP5000 S QV, Anniversary, LP400, LP400 S, LP400 Periscopio

generation_summaries.description: The later Countach with the Quattrovalvole engine and ever-wider wings became the definitive poster car of the 1980s. The QV with its 5.2-litre four-valve V12 is the performance peak; the 25th Anniversary of 1988-90 with Horacio Pagani's body revisions is the most aerodynamically effective but the most divisive stylistically.
generation_summaries.key_variants: LP500 S, LP500 QV, QV, 25th Anniversary

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: LP400, LP400 S, LP500 S, LP5000 S QV, Anniversary, LP400 Periscopio, LP500 QV, QV, 25th Anniversary

generation_summaries.description: The Diablo succeeded the Countach and raised the supercar bar to 202mph. The Roadster is the rarest body style; the GT and GTR are the homologation specials. Audi ownership brought build quality improvements from 1998.
generation_summaries.key_variants: VT, VT Roadster, SV, SE, GT, GTR, SE30, Diablo

generation_summaries.description: The final Diablo years produced the most extreme variants -- the SV with its adjustable aerodynamics, the GTR track car, and the ultimate GT with a 6.0-litre engine and a 330 mph top speed claim. Just 80 GTs were built; they are among the most collectible Lamborghinis ever made.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Diablo SV, Diablo SV roadster, Diablo GT, Diablo GTR, Diablo VT 6.0

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: VT, VT Roadster, SV, SE, GT, GTR, SE30, Diablo, Diablo VT, Diablo SE30

generation_summaries.description: The Espada is the only four-seat Lamborghini supercar. Bertone designed a genuinely beautiful 2+2 that could carry the family at 150mph. Three series were produced; Series III offers the most refinement.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Series I, Series II, Series III, Series I, Series II, Series III

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Series I, Series II, Series III

generation_summaries.description: The Jalpa was Lamborghini's entry-level car in the 1980s and shared lineage with the Urraco and Silhouette. A genuine mid-engine V8 Targa for less than the price of a Countach — and now significantly undervalued.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, 3500 Jalpa, 3500 GTS

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, 3500 Jalpa, 3500 GTS

generation_summaries.description: The McLaren F1 is the greatest driver's car ever made. Three-seat central driving position, naturally aspirated V12, carbon monocoque, and no traction control. It held the production car speed record for 14 years. GTR won Le Mans in 1995.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, LM, GT, GTR, GTS, F1 road car, F1 GT, F1 LM

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, LM, GT, GTR, GTS, F1 road car, F1 GT, F1 LM, F1 GTR Le Mans, XP1 prototype

generation_summaries.description: The R32 GT-R ended BMW M3 dominance in touring car racing so comprehensively it was nicknamed Godzilla. AWD, twin-turbo RB26, and ATTESA E-TS AWD. Increasingly valuable and Japan is now releasing export approvals.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT-R, V-Spec, Nismo

generation_summaries.description: The R33 GT-R is the bridge between the legendary R32 and the iconic R34. Often overlooked, it is the most driver-friendly of the trio — wider track, better balanced, and increasingly undervalued. BCNR33 V-Spec examples are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT-R, V-Spec, V-Spec N1

generation_summaries.description: The R34 GT-R is the most iconic Japanese car ever made. Paul Walker's Supra competitor in Fast and Furious. Only 11,578 were built and only now becoming legal to import to the US under 25-year rule.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT-R, V-Spec, V-Spec II, V-Spec II Nur, M-Spec

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GT-R, V-Spec, Nismo, V-Spec II, V-Spec II Nur, M-Spec, V-Spec N1

generation_summaries.description: The S30 redefined what a sports car could be at its price point. Clean, light, and mechanically honest — early 240Zs are among the cleanest rising-star buys in the market.

The Z32 300ZX Twin Turbo was faster than the Ferrari 348 in contemporary tests. Japanese manufacturers' horsepower agreement limited it to 300ps officially — actual output was higher. The 2+2 sacrifices little to the 2-seater.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 2+2, 2-Seater, Twin Turbo, Non-Turbo, Convertible

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 2+2, 2-Seater, Twin Turbo, Non-Turbo, Convertible

generation_summaries.description: The Toyota 2000GT is Japan's first supercar and among the most beautiful cars of the 1960s. Only 351 were built; the two open-top Bond Girl cars are unique. Yamaha developed the twin-cam engine.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Roadster Bond Cars

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Roadster Bond Cars

generation_summaries.description: The A70 Supra established the model's performance credentials. The twin-turbo 7M-GTE produces 232bhp and the long bonnet/short deck proportions previewed the legendary A80. The Turbo A is the performance variant. Increasing collector interest as the A80 becomes unaffordable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Supra Turbo, Turbo A, NA

generation_summaries.description: The A80 Supra with twin-turbo 2JZ engine is the most tuneable sports car ever made. Standard cars produce 320bhp but the engine can be taken to 1,000bhp on stock internals. Pure manual TT examples command significant premiums.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Twin Turbo, Non-Turbo, Targa

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Twin Turbo, Non-Turbo, Targa, Supra Turbo, Turbo A, NA

generation_summaries.description: The FJ40 is the most iconic Land Cruiser and one of the most collectable 4x4s. Simple, unstoppable, and endlessly restorable. Clean examples are increasingly rare as the restomod movement devours survivors.
generation_summaries.key_variants: FJ40, FJ45, BJ40, HJ40

generation_summaries.description: The 80 Series Land Cruiser is the sweet spot of the nameplate — more refined than the FJ40 but without the computer complexity of later generations. Coil springs all round, locking diffs, and a bulletproof drivetrain. The VX Limited with full options is the collector target. Values rising sharply.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GX, VX, VX Limited, FZJ80, HDJ80

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: FJ40, FJ45, BJ40, HJ40, GX, VX, VX Limited, FZJ80, HDJ80

generation_summaries.description: The NSX was designed with Ayrton Senna's input and proved a naturally aspirated V6 could deliver supercar performance with daily reliability. Manual Type S and Type R variants are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, T (Targa), Type S, Type S Zero, Type R

generation_summaries.description: The NA2 NSX-R is the ultimate expression of the original NSX. Weight reduced by over 100kg through extensive use of carbon and titanium. Forged pistons, close-ratio gearbox, high-downforce bodywork. Only 200 were made for the Japanese domestic market.
generation_summaries.key_variants: NSX-R, Type R

generation_summaries.description: Just five NSX-R GTs were built for Super GT racing homologation — each with 600bhp, sequential gearbox, full aero package, and titanium components throughout. Effectively a fully developed racing NSX with number plates.
generation_summaries.key_variants: NSX-R GT

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, T (Targa), Type S, Type S Zero, Type R, NSX-R, NSX-R GT

generation_summaries.description: The Stratos is the most purpose-built rally car ever made road-legal. Using the Ferrari Dino V6, it won the World Rally Championship three consecutive times. The road car is essentially a homologation device.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Stradale, HF, Zero Concept, Stradale, HF, Alitalia livery, Marlboro livery

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Stradale, HF, Zero Concept, Alitalia livery, Marlboro livery

generation_summaries.description: The Lancia Delta HF Integrale is the definitive homologation supercar of the 1980s and early 1990s. Six consecutive WRC Manufacturers' Championships from 1987 to 1992 give it a competition record unmatched in rallying history. The road cars are direct descendants of the rally machines -- turbocharged 2.0-litre four-cylinder, four-wheel drive, and a chassis tuned by Abarth engineers. The Integrale 8V is the raw original; the 16V gains power and composure; the Evo I sharpened the aerodynamics with flared arches; and the Evo II is the ultimate road specification with 215 bhp and the widest bodywork. The Finale Edizione -- 250 in five colours -- is the last and most collectible of all. Rust is the enemy; documented, rust-free examples command strong and rising premiums.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Integrale 8V, Integrale 16V, Integrale Evo I, Integrale Evo II, Integrale Evo II Finale Edizione, HF Turbo

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Integrale 8V, Integrale 16V, Integrale Evo I, Integrale Evo II, Integrale Evo II Finale Edizione, HF Turbo

generation_summaries.description: The 037 was the last rear-wheel drive car to win the WRC. Built around a central monocoque with a supercharged engine behind the driver, it defeated the Quattro on loose surfaces. Road cars are homologation specials.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Stradale, Rally, 037 Stradale, 037 rally car

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Stradale, Rally, 037 Stradale, 037 rally car

generation_summaries.description: The GTA (Gran Turismo Alleggerita) is the lightweight racing version of the Giulia Sprint. Aluminium bodywork, twin-plug head, and close-ratio gearbox. It dominated European Touring Car racing for years.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTA, GTA SA, GTAM, GTA, GTA 1300 Junior, GTA SA, GTA racing

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GTA, GTA SA, GTAM, GTA 1300 Junior, GTA racing

generation_summaries.description: The Series 1 Spider Duetto — round-tail design — is the most beautiful Alfa roadster. Made famous by The Graduate. Later series are more refined but the Duetto remains the collector target.

The Montreal combined Bertone styling with a detuned Formula 1 V8. Complex, temperamental, and magnificent — it is one of the most charismatic grand tourers of the 1970s and significantly undervalued.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Montreal

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Montreal

generation_summaries.description: Only 18 were built. The 33 Stradale is widely considered the most beautiful car ever made. Franco Scaglione's body over the Type 33 racing chassis resulted in a road car of extraordinary rarity and beauty.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, 33 Stradale

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, 33 Stradale

generation_summaries.description: The Type 35 is the most successful racing car in history, with over 2,000 race victories. Ettore Bugatti's masterpiece combined engineering and artistry. The supercharged 35B and 35C are the most powerful variants.

The Type 57 is the pinnacle of pre-war grand touring. The Atlantic coupe, with just four originals built, is the most valuable car in existence. Jean Bugatti designed the body; the engine is pure Ettore.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 57, 57S, 57C, 57SC, Atlantic, Atalante

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 57, 57S, 57C, 57SC, Atlantic, Atalante

generation_summaries.description: Built to revive Bugatti, the EB110 was a technological tour de force — 60-valve quad-turbo V12, all-wheel drive, carbon chassis. Michael Schumacher owned one. The company went bankrupt before reaching its potential.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT, SS

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GT, SS

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.1 L Flat-4,1.2 L Flat-4,1.5 L Flat-4,1.6 L Flat-4
generation_summaries.description: The most produced car in history. Pre-1967 oval-window and split-window bugs are the collector targets. Cabriolets are desirable in all years. Cal-look and Baja builds are distinct collectible sub-cultures.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Split Window, Oval Window, Standard, Cabriolet, Karmann Cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Split Window, Oval Window, Standard, Cabriolet, Karmann Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The original Golf GTI invented the hot hatch genre. Simple, light, and fun — it combined everyday practicality with genuine driving pleasure. Campaign and Pirelli special editions are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1600, 1800, Campaign, Pirelli, Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The Mk2 GTI refined the original formula with a wider body, greater refinement, and the addition of the 16V twin-cam engine. The G60 supercharged variant is the performance pick. The Campaign Edition and Colour Concept specials are the collector targets. The most complete hot hatch of the 1980s.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTI 8V, GTI 16V, GTI G60, Campaign Edition, Rallye Golf

generation_summaries.description: The Mk3 GTI is the forgotten hot hatch — heavier than its predecessors and criticised on launch for losing the GTI edge. The VR6 variant transformed it into something special: 174bhp, a narrow-angle six-cylinder, and genuine grand touring ability in a family hatchback. Now undervalued and rising.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTI 8V, GTI VR6, VR6, GTI Anniversary

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1600, 1800, Campaign, Pirelli, Cabriolet, GTI 8V, GTI 16V, GTI G60, Campaign Edition, Rallye Golf

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.2 L Flat-4,1.5 L Flat-4,1.6 L Flat-4
generation_summaries.description: The Karmann Ghia combined VW Beetle mechanicals with an Italian-influenced body by Ghia and coachbuilt quality from Karmann. Convertibles are the most desirable; early 1955–59 models with the larger rear window command premiums.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Coupe, Convertible, Type 34 Razor-Edge

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Coupe, Convertible, Type 34 Razor-Edge

generation_summaries.description: The Cosmo 110S was the world's first twin-rotor production car. Mazda's first sports car, it debuted rotary technology that would define the brand for 50 years. Series I cars from 1967–68 are the most desirable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Series I, Series II

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Series I, Series II

generation_summaries.description: The first-generation RX-7 is the purest rotary sports car. Light, balanced, and beautiful, the FB rewards the enthusiast driver. Turbo models are the performance pick; GSL-SE the touring choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, GS, GS-E, GSL, GSL-SE, Turbo

generation_summaries.description: The FD RX-7 is the definitive Mazda sports car. Sequential twin turbos, near-perfect weight distribution, and extraordinary chassis dynamics. Apex seal reliability improved in later production. A modern classic.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Base, R2, Touring, Type RB, Spirit R

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, GS, GS-E, GSL, GSL-SE, Turbo, Base, R2, Touring, Type RB

generation_summaries.description: The original Land Rover established the template for the utilitarian 4x4. Early 80-inch cars are the most historic; 86 and 88-inch models are more usable. Centre-steer prototypes exist but were never produced.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 80 inch, 86 inch, 88 inch, Station Wagon, 80-inch, 86-inch, 107-inch, Series I Station Wagon

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 80 inch, 86 inch, 88 inch, Station Wagon, 80-inch, 86-inch, 107-inch, Series I Station Wagon

generation_summaries.description: The Series II refined the original with a wider track and more powerful engine. The IIA introduced the 2.25-litre engine that defined Land Rovers for decades. Station Wagon examples are the most usable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 88 inch, 109 inch, Station Wagon, Forward Control, Series II 88, Series II 109, Series IIA, Safari

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 88 inch, 109 inch, Station Wagon, Forward Control, Series II 88, Series II 109, Series IIA, Safari

generation_summaries.description: The Defender is the most capable production 4x4 ever made. Final year 2015 cars command premiums; early 90s V8s are sought after for restomods. Heritage-spec and SVX limited editions are collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 90, 110, 130, Station Wagon, Hard Top, SVX, Heritage, Defender 90

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 90, 110, 130, Station Wagon, Hard Top, SVX, Heritage, Defender 90, Defender 110, Defender 130

generation_summaries.description: The Pantera combined Italian styling with American Ford V8 muscle. Sold through Ford dealers in the US, it was affordable supercar ownership. GTS and GT5-S variants are the performance picks. Elvis Presley shot his.

generation_summaries.description: The Mangusta (Italian for mongoose — mongoose beats cobra) was designed as a Shelby Cobra killer. Giugiaro styled it with iconic butterfly engine covers. Only 401 were made and the handling is challenging.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, 289, 302, 5.0 Ford V8, early production

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, 289, 302, 5.0 Ford V8, early production

generation_summaries.description: The P1800 is Volvo's sports car — made famous by Roger Moore in The Saint. The 1800ES shooting brake of 1971–73 is increasingly sought after. Irv Gordon's example holds the world record for highest mileage.

The DS was 15 years ahead of its time. Hydropneumatic suspension, disc brakes, and space-age styling revolutionised what a car could be. The presidential Cabriolet is the rarest variant; Décapotable conversions are exceptional.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 19, 20, 21, 23, Décapotable, ID, Break

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 19, 20, 21, 23, Décapotable, ID, Break

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.7 L Maserati V6,3.0 L Maserati V6
generation_summaries.description: The SM combined Citroën's hydropneumatic sophistication with a Maserati V6 — the most exotic French car ever made. Self-centring power steering and an extraordinary ride. Complexity rewards patience.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Carburateur, Injection, Opera

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Carburateur, Injection, Opera

generation_summaries.description: The 2CV was designed to put France on wheels — minimum cost, maximum practicality. The Charleston and Dolly special editions are the collector picks. The Sahara with two engines is extraordinarily rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, AZU Van, Sahara, Charleston, Dolly

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, AZU Van, Sahara, Charleston, Dolly

generation_summaries.description: The Nuova 500 is Italy's answer to the Mini — the car that mobilised a nation. The Abarth 595 and 695 variants are serious performance cars in a tiny package. Giardiniera estate versions are remarkably practical.
generation_summaries.key_variants: N, D, F, L, R, Giardiniera, Abarth 595, Abarth 695

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: N, D, F, L, R, Giardiniera, Abarth 595, Abarth 695, 500 N, 500 D

generation_summaries.description: The 124 Spider is the most successful Italian roadster ever made. Pininfarina bodywork over a capable twin-cam platform. Abarth-prepared versions competed successfully in rallying.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1400, 1600, 1800, 2000, Abarth Rally, 1.4 DOHC, 1.6 DOHC, 1.8 DOHC

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1400, 1600, 1800, 2000, Abarth Rally, 1.4 DOHC, 1.6 DOHC, 1.8 DOHC, 2.0 fuel injection, Abarth

generation_summaries.description: The Fiat Dino used a shared Ferrari Dino V6 engine — produced by Fiat to meet Ferrari's homologation requirement. The 2.4 Spider is the most desirable; the coupe by Bertone is equally beautiful.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Spider 2000, Coupe 2000, Spider 2400, Coupe 2400

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Spider 2000, Coupe 2000, Spider 2400, Coupe 2400

generation_summaries.description: The Eldorado name ran from 1953 to 2002 across radically different cars. The 1953 Eldorado is among the finest American convertibles. The 1967 front-wheel drive Eldorado pioneered the personal luxury segment.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1953 Convertible, 1957 Biarritz, 1967 FWD, Biarritz, Brougham, Biarritz, base, hardtop

generation_summaries.description: The 1959-60 Eldorado with its iconic fins represents the apex of American chrome-era excess. The Biarritz convertible in these years is one of the most photographed American cars. The 1967 transition to front-wheel drive was a landmark engineering moment.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Biarritz, Brougham, convertible, hardtop

generation_summaries.description: The 1967 Eldorado introduced front-wheel drive to the American luxury segment. The 1970 with the 500 cubic inch engine -- the largest production displacement in American history at the time -- is an engineering landmark. The final 1976 convertible is the last Cadillac ragtop for 28 years.
generation_summaries.key_variants: base, Biarritz, convertible, Custom Biarritz, 500 ci

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1953 Convertible, 1957 Biarritz, 1967 FWD, Biarritz, Brougham, base, hardtop, convertible, Custom Biarritz, 500 ci

generation_summaries.description: The Allante was flown Pininfarina bodies from Italy for assembly in Detroit. The final 1993 Northstar engine transformed the car. Regarded as a failure at launch, quality 1993 examples are now undervalued.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Northstar

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Northstar

generation_summaries.description: 4-4-2 stood for four-barrel carb, four-speed gearbox, dual exhausts. The W-30 and W-32 performance packages are the collector targets. Hurst/Olds editions are particularly desirable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: W-30, W-32, Hurst/Olds, Holiday, 442, L69 Tri-Power, W-30, convertible

generation_summaries.description: The 1969-70 442 W-30 is the most desirable Oldsmobile muscle car. The force-air induction 400 with its red plastic inner fenders and cold-air hood is a strong performer. The 455 of 1971 produced monster torque but was the last year before compression cuts.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 442, W-30, W-32, 455, convertible, Holiday Coupe

generation_summaries.description: The 1972-80 442 transitioned to an appearance package on the Cutlass, losing performance credibility but gaining personal luxury buyers. The 1970 455 Indy Pace Car replica and 1972 Hurst/Olds editions are the rare performance highlights of the period.

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: W-30, W-32, Hurst/Olds, Holiday, 442, L69 Tri-Power, convertible, 455, Holiday Coupe, 442 package

generation_summaries.description: The 1966 Toronado was the first American front-wheel drive car since the Cord 810. The styling by David North is dramatic and forward-looking. The 1966–67 cars are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1966, 1967, 1968, Brougham, base, Custom, W-34, GT

generation_summaries.description: The 1971-78 Toronado grew larger and more formal, embracing the personal luxury direction pioneered by its first generation. The XSR sport variant with its distinctive bodywork is a rare and underappreciated piece of Oldsmobile design.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Custom, Brougham, XSR, 455

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1966, 1967, 1968, Brougham, base, Custom, W-34, GT, XSR, 455

generation_summaries.description: The Buick Gran Sport, especially the Stage 1 455, is the most underrated muscle car of its era. The 455 Stage 1 produced more torque than any contemporary V8. Skylark GS 455 Stage 1 examples are significantly undervalued.

generation_summaries.description: Bill Mitchell's 1963 Riviera is considered the finest American design of the postwar era. The combination of Rolls-Royce-inspired lines with American V8 power set a template for the personal luxury coupe segment.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Gran Sport, base, GS, Gran Sport

generation_summaries.description: The 1966-70 Riviera Gran Sport with the 465 lb-ft 455 is a sleek, underrated personal luxury muscle car. The 1970 in particular represents the last of the clean-body design before federalized bumpers arrived.
generation_summaries.key_variants: base, Gran Sport, GS 455

generation_summaries.description: The 1971-73 Boat Tail Riviera is one of the most polarizing and now celebrated American designs of the era -- a dramatic fastback with a rear "boat tail" tapering to a central point. Stage 1 examples are the performance pinnacle.
generation_summaries.key_variants: base, Stage 1, 455 Stage 1

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Gran Sport, base, GS, GS 455, Stage 1, 455 Stage 1

generation_summaries.description: The AMX was AMC's two-seat muscle car — one of only three true two-seat American production cars alongside the Cobra and Corvette. The 390 and Go Package variants are the collector targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 390, 401, Go Package, 390, 343, Go Pack, Big Bad, Scrambler

generation_summaries.description: The 1971-74 AMX became a trim level on the Javelin rather than a standalone model. The Javelin AMX with the 401 and Go Package is the collector target -- more power, aggressive body lines, and AMC's most complete performance package.
generation_summaries.key_variants: AMX, 401 Go Package, 360, 304

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 390, 401, Go Package, 343, Go Pack, Big Bad, Scrambler, AMX, 401 Go Package, 360

generation_summaries.description: The Javelin was AMC's pony car challenger. The Trans-Am racing programme produced real performance hardware. Pierre Cardin and Hurst editions stand out. Often overlooked relative to Mustang and Camaro.
generation_summaries.key_variants: SST, Go Package, Trans-Am, Pierre Cardin, AMX/Javelin, base, SST, 390

generation_summaries.description: The 1971-74 Javelin AMX with the new body and 401 V8 is the performance apex of the AMC pony car. The Pierre Cardin edition is a rare factory luxury trim; the Trans-Am racing heritage cars provide genuine racing provenance.
generation_summaries.key_variants: AMX, Pierre Cardin, Go Package, 401, 360, Trans-Am

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: SST, Go Package, Trans-Am, Pierre Cardin, AMX/Javelin, base, 390, 343 Go Pack, Big Bad, AMX

generation_summaries.description: The Elan defined the lightweight British sports car. Colin Chapman's backbone chassis and fibreglass body produced a roadster of extraordinary agility. The Sprint is the ultimate development; the +2 the practical choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: S1, S2, S3, S4, Sprint, Plus 2

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: S1, S2, S3, S4, Sprint, Plus 2

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L Turbo I4,3.5 L Twin-Turbo V8
generation_summaries.description: The Esprit Turbo was a proper supercar in a Giugiaro suit. The V8 GT of 1996 onward raised performance to match Ferrari. The white S1 from The Spy Who Loved Me is the cultural icon.
generation_summaries.key_variants: S1, S2, S2.2, Turbo, HC, SE, Sport 300, V8

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.2 L turbocharged I4,3.5 L twin-turbo V8
generation_summaries.description: The Esprit V8 of 1996-2004 is the most capable Lotus Esprit -- twin turbocharged, 350 bhp, and with handling refined over two decades of development. The Sport 350 and Sport 300 are track-focused limited editions. The final cars represent a complete sports car package that rivals far more expensive machinery.
generation_summaries.key_variants: SE, S4, S4s, GT3, V8, Sport 350, Sport 300, Final Edition

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: S1, S2, S2.2, Turbo, HC, SE, Sport 300, V8, V8 GT, S3

generation_summaries.description: The S1 Elise reset expectations for what a lightweight sports car could be. Extruded aluminium chassis, sub-700kg weight, and telepathic handling. The 111S is the performance variant; standard cars are the driving purist's choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, 111S, Sport 135, Sport 160, base, Sport 135, Sport 160, 111S

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.8 L Toyota I4,1.8 L supercharged I4
generation_summaries.description: The S2 Elise with Toyota power is the definitive Elise -- reliable, fast, and with handling that makes experienced drivers feel like heroes. The 111R with the 192 bhp VVTL-i engine and the supercharged SC are the performance picks; the Sport 190 and Cup 220 are track-focused limited editions.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 111R, SC, Sport 190, Cup 220, 111, S2 base, Club Racer

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, 111S, Sport 135, Sport 160, base, 111R, SC, Sport 190, Cup 220, 111

generation_summaries.description: The Ghibli is the most beautiful Maserati ever made — Giorgetto Giugiaro's masterpiece for the company. The Spyder is exceptionally rare at 125 built. A 4.9 SS example is among the most desirable Italian cars of its era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 4.7, 4.9, 4.9 SS, Spyder, 4.7, 4.9, Spyder 4.7, Spyder 4.9

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 4.7, 4.9, 4.9 SS, Spyder, Spyder 4.7, Spyder 4.9

generation_summaries.description: The Bora was Maserati's first mid-engine road car, designed by Giugiaro and featuring a Citroën hydraulic system. Shares architecture with the Merak. The 4.9 variant is more powerful and the collector preference.
The Merak shared the Bora's body and mid-engine layout but used a smaller V6. The SS variant is the most desirable. Citroën hydraulics can be complex but the cars are rewarding when properly sorted.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Merak, SS, 2000 GT, Merak, Merak SS, 2000 GT

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Merak, SS, 2000 GT, Merak SS

generation_summaries.description: The Evo VI Tommi Mäkinen Edition is the most desirable Lancer Evolution. Built to celebrate four consecutive WRC driver titles, it features a titanium turbo and front-facing fog lights. TME examples command significant premiums.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS, GSR, Tommi Makinen Edition

generation_summaries.description: The Evo IX was the final chapter of the 4G63-powered Evo era — the engine that defined the nameplate. The MR (Mitsubishi Racing) variant with twin-clutch SST previewed the future; the RS with manual gearbox preserved the past. The last Evo worth arguing about.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS, GSR, MR, FQ-360

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: RS, GSR, Tommi Makinen Edition, MR, FQ-360

generation_summaries.description: The 3000GT VR-4 was the most technically complex Japanese sports car of its era — active aerodynamics, all-wheel drive, all-wheel steering, and twin turbos. The Spyder convertible is exceptionally rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: VR-4, SL, Base, Spyder VR-4

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: VR-4, SL, Base, Spyder VR-4

generation_summaries.description: The GC8 STI is the rally homologation hero. Colin McRae and Richard Burns won WRC titles in cars based on this platform. Version VI and RA-R examples are the collector targets. Right-hand drive import demand is growing.
generation_summaries.key_variants: WRX, STI, Type R, RA, Version I–VI, 22B

generation_summaries.description: The GD chassis brought the STI to the US market for the first time in 2004. The Blobeye (2004–05) and Hawkeye (2006–07) facelifts are the collector targets. The R205 and S204 Japanese-market specials are extraordinarily rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: WRX, STI, Spec C, R205, S204

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: WRX, STI, Type R, RA, Version I–VI, 22B, Spec C, R205, S204

generation_summaries.description: The TR3A was the first British production car with disc brakes and the first to offer them as standard. Simple, tough, and rewarding, it dominated American sports car racing in the late 1950s.
generation_summaries.key_variants: TR3, TR3A, TR3B

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: TR3, TR3A, TR3B

generation_summaries.description: The TR6 is the last of the traditional Triumph roadsters. Karmann-styled with a 150bhp straight-six, it remains one of the most accessible British classic sports cars. US-spec fuel injection cars need upgrading.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, US Spec, PI, TR6 UK, TR6 US, 150bhp TR6, fuel injection TR6

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, US Spec, PI, TR6 UK, TR6 US, 150bhp TR6, fuel injection TR6

generation_summaries.description: The Stag had one of the most beautiful bodies of any 1970s car. The V8 engine's cooling issues are legendary but modern fixes make them reliable. Well-maintained examples are among the most usable British classics.
generation_summaries.key_variants: MK1, MK2, Auto, Stag Mk1, Stag Mk2, automatic, manual

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: MK1, MK2, Auto, Stag Mk1, Stag Mk2, automatic, manual

generation_summaries.description: The MGA replaced the boxy T-series with a modern aerodynamic body. The Twin Cam is the performance variant — complex but rewarding when right. The 1600 Mk II is the most usable standard car.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1500, Twin Cam, 1600, 1600 Mk II, Coupe, MGA 1500, MGA Twin Cam, Twin Cam Coupe

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.6 L I4,1.6 L Mk II I4
generation_summaries.description: The MGA 1600 Mk II with the twin-cam option deleted gave a more reliable but still sporting package. The De Luxe coupe with Twin Cam running gear in the pushrod body is the ultimate MGA variant -- all the reliability of the pushrod with uprated brakes and wheels.
generation_summaries.key_variants: MGA 1600, MGA 1600 Mk II, MGA De Luxe Coupe, MGA 1600 Coupe

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1500, Twin Cam, 1600, 1600 Mk II, Coupe, MGA 1500, MGA Twin Cam, Twin Cam Coupe, Twin Cam Roadster, MGA 1600

generation_summaries.description: The MGB is the world's most successful British sports car. Monocoque construction, good performance, and affordable parts make it the ideal introduction to classic motoring. Rubber-bumper cars are cheapest; chrome-bumper most desirable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Roadster, GT, GT V8, Jubilee, Limited Edition, Roadster, GT, GTV8

generation_summaries.description: The rubber-bumper MGB is the Marmite MG -- purists dislike the raised ride height and black bumpers imposed by US regulations, but these are the most affordable entry to MGB ownership. The 1980 Limited Edition in bronze or black with gold stripes is an attractive final chapter.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Roadster, GT, Limited Edition bronze, Limited Edition black

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Roadster, GT, GT V8, Jubilee, Limited Edition, GTV8, MGC GT, chrome bumper, Limited Edition bronze, Limited Edition black

generation_summaries.description: The TD was the first MG designed for left-hand drive and the car that established the MG brand in America. Independent front suspension improved the T-series chassis. The TF that followed is more refined but rarer.
generation_summaries.key_variants: TD, TD Mk2, TD, TD Mk II

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: TD, TD Mk2, TD Mk II

generation_summaries.description: The 3000 Mk I introduced disc brakes and 2.9-litre power; the Mk II added a triple SU carburetor option for the competition variant. These are the most sporting of the big Healeys -- lighter and less refined than the Mk III but with more raw appeal.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 3000 Mk I BT7, 3000 Mk I BJ7, 3000 Mk II, 3000 Mk II BJ7

generation_summaries.description: The 3000 Mk III is the finest of the Big Healeys. The Phase II interior with wood dashboard and twin SU carburettors producing 148bhp. Rally-proven and genuinely fast, these are among the most usable classic British sports cars.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mk III Phase I, Mk III Phase II, 3000 Mk III BJ8, Phase 1, Phase 2

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Mk III Phase I, Mk III Phase II, 3000 Mk III BJ8, Phase 1, Phase 2, 3000 Mk I BT7, 3000 Mk I BJ7, 3000 Mk II, 3000 Mk II BJ7

generation_summaries.description: The Frogeye Sprite is the most endearing British sports car. Fixed headlights in the bonnet, no external boot opening, and minimal equipment — just driving pleasure. Shared Bugeye DNA with early Midgets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mk I Frogeye, Mk II, Mk III, Mk IV, Frogeye, Mk I

generation_summaries.description: The Mk II onward Sprite lost the frogeye headlamps but gained proper wind-up windows and a more sophisticated interior. The Mk III and IV with the 1275 A-series are the most capable; these cars are interchangeable with the Midget and share all running gear.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mk II, Mk III, Mk IV, 1275 Sprite

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Mk I Frogeye, Mk II, Mk III, Mk IV, Frogeye, Mk I, 1275 Sprite

generation_summaries.engine_options: 5.4 L Chevrolet V8,6.5 L Chevrolet V8,5.8 L Ford V8
generation_summaries.description: The Iso Grifo combined Bertone styling with American V8 reliability. Giotto Bizzarrini's chassis gave it handling to match the Ferrari 275 GTB. The Can Am Series II with 7-litre Corvette engine is the most brutal variant.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Series I, Series II, 7 Litre, GL 350, GL 365, Can Am 7 litre

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Series I, Series II, 7 Litre, GL 350, GL 365, Can Am 7 litre
