generation_summaries.description: The Iso Rivolta is the grand touring companion to the Grifo. Bertone's four-seat body over the same Bizzarrini chassis offers comfort without sacrificing the V8 character. Significantly undervalued relative to Italian competitors.
generation_summaries.key_variants: IR300, Fidia, IR 300, IR 340

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: IR300, Fidia, IR 300, IR 340

generation_summaries.description: Raymond Loewy designed the Avanti as a last-ditch attempt to save Studebaker. The supercharged R3 broke 29 land speed records. After Studebaker closed, the design continued under Avanti Motor Corporation.
The Sonett III was Saab's last attempt at a sports car. Styled by Sergio Coggiola with a fibreglass body, it used a Ford Taunus V4 engine. The rarest and most refined of the Sonett series.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Sonett II, Sonett V4, Sonett III

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Sonett II, Sonett V4, Sonett III

generation_summaries.description: The Blower Bentley is the most famous pre-war British racing car. Birkin's supercharger was opposed by W.O. Bentley himself. Among the most desirable cars ever made.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Le Mans, Birkin Blower, Road Car, 4.5L Supercharged, 4.5L Blower, Le Mans, Le Mans replica

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Le Mans, Birkin Blower, Road Car, 4.5L Supercharged, 4.5L Blower, Le Mans replica

generation_summaries.description: The R-Type Continental was the fastest four-seat car in the world in 1952. H.J. Mulliner's fastback body is a masterpiece of elegant engineering. Only 208 were built and all are documented.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, H.J. Mulliner, R-Type Continental, fastback, drophead

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, H.J. Mulliner, R-Type Continental, fastback, drophead

generation_summaries.description: The Frazer Nash Le Mans Replica is the ultimate expression of chain-drive sports car engineering. Just 34 were built with Bristol engines. These cars finished 3rd overall at Le Mans in 1949.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mk I, Mk II

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Mk I, Mk II

generation_summaries.description: The Allard J2 was the Cobra before the Cobra — massive American V8 in a lightweight British roadster. Sydney Allard drove one to third overall at Le Mans in 1950. A direct inspiration for Carroll Shelby.
generation_summaries.key_variants: J2, J2X

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: J2, J2X

generation_summaries.description: The 912 used the 911 body with an economical four-cylinder engine from the 356. Originally dismissed as a lesser 911, early short-wheelbase examples are now recognised as pure, lightweight driving machines. The rare 912E of 1976 used a VW engine.

The 928 was Ferdinand Piëch's vision of a 911 successor — front-engine V8 grand tourer. It never replaced the 911 but earned a devoted following. The GTS is the definitive final variant. Originally driven by Tom Cruise in Risky Business.

The 928 GTS is the final and finest expression of the front-engined GT Porsche -- 350 hp, wider body, and the most resolved version of the design. Values have climbed sharply as the model has been re-evaluated; low-mileage GTS coupes in Guards Red or Grand Prix White are the targets.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTS, GTS 5-speed, GTS automatic

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: S, S4, GT, GTS, 928, 928 S, 928 S4, 928 S4 5-speed, 928 S4 automatic, GTS 5-speed

generation_summaries.description: The 924 was Porsche's entry-level car and initially derided for its VW/Audi origins. The 924 Turbo is a genuine performance car; the 924 Carrera GT and GTS are homologation specials of extraordinary rarity. Le Mans class winners.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 924, 924 Turbo, 924 Carrera GT, 924 Carrera GTS, 924S

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 924, 924 Turbo, 924 Carrera GT, 924 Carrera GTS, 924S

generation_summaries.description: The 968 was the final development of the 944/924 lineage — lighter, faster, and better in every way. Its 3.0-litre four-cylinder was the largest naturally aspirated four in any production car. Club Sport is the driver's car; Cabriolet the rarest.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 968, 968 Cabriolet, 968 Club Sport, 968 Turbo S

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 968, 968 Cabriolet, 968 Club Sport, 968 Turbo S

generation_summaries.description: The Carrera GT used a Formula 1-derived V10 and a ceramic clutch that earned a fearsome reputation. Paul Walker died in one in 2013, intensifying its cultural notoriety. Carbon monocoque, pushrod suspension — pure racing car technology on the road.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The 550 Spyder is one of the most significant racing cars Porsche ever built. James Dean died in his on September 30, 1955 — serial number 550-0055. Lightweight, mid-engine, and devastatingly effective against far more powerful machinery.

The 718 RSK and RS60/RS61 were Porsche's factory weapons at Le Mans, Targa Florio, and the Nürburgring. Stirling Moss drove them to numerous victories. Fewer than 22 were built and all are accounted for.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RSK, RS60, RS61, 718 W-RS

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: RSK, RS60, RS61, 718 W-RS

generation_summaries.description: The S2000 was Honda's 50th anniversary car and possibly the finest front-engine, rear-drive roadster ever made. The 9,000rpm F20C engine is a masterpiece. AP1 with the high-revving 240bhp engine is the enthusiast pick; AP2 more usable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: AP1, AP2, Club Racer

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: AP1, AP2, Club Racer

generation_summaries.description: The ST165 was Toyota's first all-wheel drive Celica and their first WRC competitor. Juha Kankkunen won the 1990 WRC drivers championship in the closely related ST185, but the ST165 laid the groundwork. Group A homologation required 5,000 road cars — all are desirable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT-Four, Carlos Sainz Edition

generation_summaries.description: The ST185 won the WRC manufacturers title in 1993 and 1994 with Carlos Sainz and Didier Auriol. The road car matched Group A spec with all-wheel drive, viscous LSDs, and intercooled turbo. The Carlos Sainz Limited Edition with 235bhp is the definitive variant.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT-Four, Carlos Sainz Limited Edition, RC

generation_summaries.description: The ST205 Celica GT-Four was Toyota's WRC homologation weapon. Carlos Sainz and Didier Auriol drove it to titles. The road car repackaged full rally hardware — all-wheel drive, intercooled turbo, and limited-slip differentials — in a practical coupe.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT-Four, WRC, RC

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GT-Four, WRC, RC, Carlos Sainz Edition, Carlos Sainz Limited Edition

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.6 L B6 I4,1.8 L BP I4
generation_summaries.description: The original Miata revived the lightweight British roadster formula with Japanese reliability. Colin Chapman's ghost in a Mazda badge. Simple, balanced, and joyful — the most raced production car in history. Special editions and low-mileage survivors command premiums.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1.6, 1.8, M Edition, R Package, Limited, Mazdaspeed

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.8 L BP I4,1.8 L BP Turbo
generation_summaries.description: The NB refined the NA formula with a crisper body and optional power-retractable hardtop. The Mazdaspeed Miata turbocharged version is the performance pick. NB2 facelift cars with revised headlights are the most desirable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: NB1, NB2, Mazdaspeed, 10th Anniversary, SE

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1.6, 1.8, M Edition, R Package, Limited, Mazdaspeed, NB1, NB2, 10th Anniversary, SE

generation_summaries.description: The DC5 Type R is arguably the greatest front-wheel drive car ever made. The K20A engine to 8,400rpm, close-ratio six-speed, helical limited-slip differential, and weight trimmed to the bone. Championship White examples are the collector standard.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Type R, Type S

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Type R, Type S

generation_summaries.description: The AW11 was Toyota's first mid-engine road car and a landmark in affordable sports car design. The supercharged SC version is the performance pick with 145bhp. Pop-up headlights, T-bar roof option, and near-perfect mid-engine balance. The original poor man's Ferrari.
generation_summaries.key_variants: N/A, SC (Supercharged), T-Bar

generation_summaries.description: The SW20 transformed the MR2 into a genuine supercar rival. The turbocharged 3S-GTE produces 245bhp in later Revision 5 cars. Early snap-oversteer reputation was addressed through three revisions — Revision 5 (1994+) is the definitive car. The Turbo is the collector target.
generation_summaries.key_variants: N/A, Turbo, Revision 1, Revision 3, Revision 5

generation_summaries.description: The W30 MR2 Spyder is the mid-engine roadster Lotus could never quite make affordable. Light, balanced, and tossable — the VVTL-i engine variant is the performance pick. Rising sharply as buyers discover what Miata money can get in mid-engine form.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, VVTL-i

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, VVTL-i, N/A, SC (Supercharged), T-Bar, Turbo, Revision 1, Revision 3, Revision 5

generation_summaries.description: The 360 Modena was Ferrari's first all-aluminium production car and a quantum leap from the F355 it replaced. Pininfarina's body is more dramatic; the 400bhp V8 more tractable. The Challenge Stradale is the stripped track variant; Spider the open-air choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Modena, Spider, Challenge Stradale, 360 Modena, 360 Spider, 360 Challenge Stradale

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Modena, Spider, Challenge Stradale, 360 Modena, 360 Spider, 360 Challenge Stradale

generation_summaries.description: The 430 Scuderia stripped the F430 to its essentials — 100kg lighter, 510bhp, carbon ceramic brakes, and the E-Diff from the 430 Challenge. The Scuderia Spider 16M followed in 2009. Just 499 of each built. The benchmark lightweight Ferrari of its era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Scuderia, Spider 16M

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Scuderia, Spider 16M

generation_summaries.description: Named after the founder, the Enzo applied Formula 1 technology directly to a road car — carbon fibre body, semi-automatic transmission, carbon ceramic brakes, active aerodynamics. 400 were planned; 399 sold through Ferrari's client list, one donated to the Vatican.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Enzo, Enzo Ferrari

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Enzo, Enzo Ferrari

generation_summaries.description: The Gallardo became Lamborghini's best-selling car of all time — and proved the company could build a reliable, usable supercar. The LP570-4 Superleggera is the driver's pick; the Spyder Performante the open-air choice. Now approaching the bottom of their depreciation curve.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Gallardo, LP560-4, LP570-4 Superleggera, Spyder, Spyder Performante, LP550-2, Gallardo, Gallardo Spyder

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Gallardo, LP560-4, LP570-4 Superleggera, Spyder, Spyder Performante, LP550-2, Gallardo Spyder, LP570-4 Spyder Performante, Sesto Elemento

generation_summaries.description: The Murciélago was the last Lamborghini developed entirely without Audi's influence. Its 6.5-litre V12 in the LP670 produces 670bhp with minimal electronic intervention. The LP670-4 SuperVeloce is the ultimate expression — just 350 built.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Murciélago, LP640, LP650-4 Roadster, LP670-4 SuperVeloce, Murcielago, Murcielago roadster, LP640, LP670-4 SV

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Murciélago, LP640, LP650-4 Roadster, LP670-4 SuperVeloce, Murcielago, Murcielago roadster, LP670-4 SV

generation_summaries.description: The original Vanquish was Aston Martin's hand-built flagship — a 190mph Grand Tourer built to confront Ferrari head-on. The 2004 Vanquish S raised power to 520bhp. The last Aston built almost entirely by hand at Newport Pagnell before production moved to Gaydon.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Vanquish, Vanquish S, Vanquish, Vanquish S, Vanquish Volante

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Vanquish, Vanquish S, Vanquish Volante

generation_summaries.description: The E60 M5 contains the S85 — a 500bhp naturally aspirated V10 derived from the M3 CSL's concept and the Williams F1 programme. Nothing else sounds or feels like it. The Touring estate variant is extraordinarily rare. SMG gearbox requires maintenance attention.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Sedan, Touring, SMG, 6-Speed Manual

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Sedan, Touring, SMG, 6-Speed Manual

generation_summaries.description: The 1M Coupe is the last BMW M car built to the original M division philosophy — minimum weight, maximum driver involvement, no compromise. The widened E82 body, S65-inspired suspension, and N54 engine made it quicker around the Nürburgring than the E60 M5. Never officially called M1.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The W204 C63 AMG contained the M156 — a 457bhp naturally aspirated 6.2-litre V8 hand-built by a single AMG technician. The last of the large naturally aspirated AMG V8s before forced induction arrived. The Black Series and Edition 507 are the collector variants.
generation_summaries.key_variants: C63 AMG, Black Series, Edition 507, Performance Package, Estate, C63 AMG, C63 AMG Black Series, C63 P30

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: C63 AMG, Black Series, Edition 507, Performance Package, Estate, C63 AMG Black Series, C63 P30

generation_summaries.description: Ford built the 2005 GT to celebrate its centenary and its Le Mans legacy. Hand-laid fibreglass over an aluminium honeycomb chassis, 550bhp supercharged V8, and retro GT40 proportions. Only 4,038 were built — all in the same two years. Values have tripled in a decade.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Heritage Edition

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Heritage Edition

generation_summaries.description: The Veyron was the first production car to break 1,000bhp and 400km/h. Its W16 engine with four turbochargers required ten radiators and a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox. Engineering excess as art. The Super Sport raised the bar to 1,200bhp and 268mph.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 16.4, Grand Sport, Super Sport, Vitesse, L'Or Blanc

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 16.4, Grand Sport, Super Sport, Vitesse, L'Or Blanc

generation_summaries.description: The B5 RS4 Avant is the original RS4 — a 380bhp biturbo V6, quattro AWD, and a six-speed manual in an estate body. Built jointly with Cosworth who developed the cylinder head. The B5 was only available as an Avant (estate) and Cabriolet convertible. Just 6,018 were made in two years. Enormously undervalued.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS4 Avant, RS4 Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The B7 RS4 is the definitive RS4 — a naturally aspirated 4.2-litre V8 producing 420bhp, quattro all-wheel drive, and a six-speed manual gearbox. The Avant estate is the understated Q-car par excellence. Porsche-designed suspension, motorsport-derived engine.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Sedan, Avant, Cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Sedan, Avant, Cabriolet, RS4 Avant, RS4 Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The 166 MM is the car that established Ferrari's legend. Barchetta (little boat) bodywork by Touring, a 2.0-litre V12, and outright victories at Le Mans and the Mille Miglia in 1949. Every surviving example is a cornerstone of automotive history.
generation_summaries.key_variants: MM Barchetta, MM Berlinetta, Inter, Barchetta, Berlinetta, Coupe

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: MM Barchetta, MM Berlinetta, Inter, Barchetta, Berlinetta, Coupe

generation_summaries.description: The 250 GT Short Wheelbase Berlinetta is the ultimate dual-purpose Ferrari — beautiful enough for the road, fast enough to win Le Mans GT class outright. Stirling Moss drove one at Goodwood. Steel and alloy body versions exist; the alloy competition cars are the most valuable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Steel body, Alloy body, SEFAC Hot Rod, California Spider SWB, SWB Berlinetta, SEFAC hot rod, Drogo Breadvan

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Steel body, Alloy body, SEFAC Hot Rod, California Spider SWB, SWB Berlinetta, SEFAC hot rod, Drogo Breadvan

generation_summaries.description: The 250 GT Cabriolet Series I and II were Pininfarina's open interpretation of the 250 GT. The Series II of 1959 onward is the more refined and collectible car. The California Spyder — open headlight version — is among the most desirable Ferraris ever made.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Series I, Series II, California Spyder

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Series I, Series II, California Spyder

generation_summaries.description: The 410 Superamerica was Ferrari's most powerful and exclusive road car of the 1950s. A 4.9-litre V12, coachbuilt body by Pininfarina or Boano, and a price three times that of a contemporary 250 GT. Built exclusively for wealthy American clients.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Series I, Series II, Series III

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Series I, Series II, Series III

generation_summaries.description: The 365 GTC/4 was Ferrari's 2+2 companion to the Daytona. Five-speed gearbox, four overhead camshafts, and side-draught carburettors under a long bonnet. Pininfarina's wedge design was ahead of its time. Only 500 built in just two years.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The 400 and 412 were Ferrari's grand touring 2+2 — the only Ferraris ever offered with an automatic gearbox as standard. Unloved for decades, they are now recognised as supremely elegant Pininfarina designs. Manual examples command significant premiums.

The 308 GT4 was the first mid-engine 2+2 Ferrari and the only Ferrari road car designed by Bertone rather than Pininfarina. Initially sold as a Dino without Ferrari badging. Its angular Bertone wedge shape divided opinion on launch; today it is recognised as a design masterpiece and significantly undervalued relative to its 308 GTB sibling.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Dino 208 GT4, 308 GT4

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Dino 208 GT4, 308 GT4

generation_summaries.description: The Mondial was Ferrari's long-running 2+2 mid-engine car — the only mid-engine Ferrari with a proper rear seat and a convertible option. The Mondial t with transverse gearbox is the most usable; the Cabriolet the most sought after. Extremely accessible entry into Ferrari ownership.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mondial 8, QV, 3.2, t, t Cabriolet, Cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Mondial 8, QV, 3.2, t, t Cabriolet, Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The 348 replaced the 328 and introduced longitudinal engine mounting and a straked side treatment echoing the Testarossa. Initially criticised for wayward handling, late cars with revised suspension are rewarding drivers. The TB and TS are the hardtop variants; the Spider the rarest.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 348 tb, 348 ts, 348 Spider, 348 Speciale, Challenge

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 348 tb, 348 ts, 348 Spider, 348 Speciale, Challenge

generation_summaries.description: The 456 was Ferrari's return to the front-engine 2+2 after the 412. A 5.5-litre V12, Pininfarina design of extraordinary elegance, and — uniquely — a manual gearbox option that commands large premiums over the automatic. The last great front-engine 2+2 of the classic era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 456 GT, 456 GTA, 456M GT, 456M GTA

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 456 GT, 456 GTA, 456M GT, 456M GTA

generation_summaries.description: The 550 Maranello marked Ferrari's return to the front-engine supercar after 23 years of mid-engine flagships. 485bhp V12, manual gearbox, and a top speed of 199mph. The Barchetta Pininfarina concept spawned a 448-unit open version. The 575M that followed added power and F1 paddle shift.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 550 Maranello, 550 Barchetta, 550 Maranello, 550 Barchetta

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 550 Maranello, 550 Barchetta

generation_summaries.description: The 575M evolved the 550 with 515bhp, updated suspension, and the option of Ferrari's F1 paddle-shift transmission alongside the traditional manual. The Superamerica introduced a unique rotating glass roof — one of the most innovative open-car solutions ever engineered.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 575M Maranello, 575M Superamerica, 575M GTC

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 575M Maranello, 575M Superamerica, 575M GTC

generation_summaries.description: The F430 replaced the 360 and raised the bar dramatically — 483bhp, E-Diff electronic differential, and a 0-100mph time under 10 seconds. The F430 Challenge race car is closely related. The Spider with its electrohydraulic roof is the open-air choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: F430, F430 Spider, F430 Challenge, F430 Scuderia, Scuderia Spider 16M, F430, F430 Spider, F430 Scuderia

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: F430, F430 Spider, F430 Challenge, F430 Scuderia, Scuderia Spider 16M, F430 16M Spider

generation_summaries.description: The 458 Italia is widely regarded as the finest Ferrari of the modern era — a naturally aspirated 570bhp V8 revving to 9,000rpm, double-wishbone suspension, and aerodynamics developed in Formula 1. The Speciale and Speciale A are the stripped track variants. The last naturally aspirated V8 Ferrari.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 458 Italia, 458 Spider, 458 Speciale, 458 Speciale A, 458 Italia, 458 Spider, 458 Speciale, 458 Speciale A

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 458 Italia, 458 Spider, 458 Speciale, 458 Speciale A

generation_summaries.description: The F12 Berlinetta produced 730bhp from its 6.3-litre V12 — the most powerful naturally aspirated V12 Ferrari road car. 0-62mph in 3.1 seconds. The TDF (Tour de France) limited edition is the stripped lightweight variant, producing 780bhp with passive aerodynamics. The last of the classic front-engine V12 lineage.
generation_summaries.key_variants: F12 Berlinetta, F12 TDF, F12 Berlinetta, F12tdf

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: F12 Berlinetta, F12 TDF, F12tdf

generation_summaries.description: LaFerrari combined a 6.3-litre V12 with a Formula 1-derived hybrid system to produce 950bhp — more than any road car Ferrari had previously made. The HY-KERS system harvested energy under braking. 499 coupes and 210 Apertas were built, each allocated to established Ferrari clients.
generation_summaries.key_variants: LaFerrari, LaFerrari Aperta, LaFerrari, LaFerrari Aperta

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: LaFerrari, LaFerrari Aperta

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.5 L ZC I4,1.6 L B16A VTEC I4
generation_summaries.description: The CR-X Si is the definitive 1980s lightweight hot hatch. Short wheelbase, near 50/50 weight distribution, and Honda's VTEC engine in late examples made it a giant-killer. The EF8 Si-R with 150bhp VTEC B16A is the collector target — fun, light, and increasingly rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Si, Si-R, HF, VXi

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Si, Si-R, HF, VXi

generation_summaries.description: The EK9 Civic Type R was the first Honda to wear the Type R badge. The B16B is the highest-revving naturally aspirated engine Honda ever fitted to a road car — 185bhp from 1.6 litres, redline at 8,200rpm. Championship White only in Japan. Becoming very collectible.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Type R, SiR

generation_summaries.description: The EP3 was the first Civic Type R built in the UK and the first to use the K20 engine. Heavier than the EK9 but significantly more powerful at 197bhp. The independent rear suspension transformed cornering balance. Red interior, bucket seats, and close-ratio six-speed standard.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Type R, Sport

generation_summaries.description: The FN2 is the last naturally aspirated Civic Type R and the most controversial — the aggressive styling divided opinion. Underneath, the K20 engine, close-ratio gearbox, and front limited-slip differential make it a fine driver's car. The last of the high-revving VTEC Type Rs.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Type R, Mugen

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Type R, SiR, Sport, Mugen

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L F20B DOHC I4,2.2 L H22A VTEC I4
generation_summaries.description: The fifth-generation Prelude was Honda's most technically sophisticated coupe — available with Active Torque Transfer System (ATTS) that actively distributed torque between front wheels for neutral cornering. The H22A VTEC engine produces 200bhp. The last and finest Prelude.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Si, VTi, ATTS, Type S

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Si, VTi, ATTS, Type S

generation_summaries.description: The Honda Beat is Japan's most collectible kei roadster. Mid-engine, rear-drive, naturally aspirated, and with a five-speed gearbox — a tiny Mazda Miata philosophy in miniature. Designed by Pininfarina, produced for only five years. Appreciating rapidly as JDM collector cars cross the 25-year rule.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The Accord Type R is one of the rarest and most overlooked Honda performance cars. Just 3,602 were built, all in Championship White. The H22A7 produces 212bhp — only available with a close-ratio six-speed manual. Front limited-slip differential and Brembo brakes standard.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Type R

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Type R

generation_summaries.description: The AE86 is the most culturally significant Japanese car ever made — 'Initial D' made it a global icon, but the reality is even better. Rear-wheel drive, 128bhp twin-cam, and a chassis of perfect simplicity. Trueno (pop-up headlights) versus Levin (fixed) is the great debate. Unmodified survivors are extraordinarily rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Trueno GT-APEX, Trueno SR, Levin GT-APEX, Levin SR, Sprinter Trueno

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Trueno GT-APEX, Trueno SR, Levin GT-APEX, Levin SR, Sprinter Trueno

generation_summaries.description: The Z30 Soarer was Toyota's flagship grand tourer — the 1UZ-FE V8 version sold as the Lexus SC400 in export markets. Electronically controlled air suspension, a V8 whisper-quiet at speed, and elegant 1990s styling. The SC400 with manual swap is the ultimate Japanese GT.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Soarer 430, Soarer 250T, Lexus SC400, Lexus SC300

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Soarer 430, Soarer 250T, Lexus SC400, Lexus SC300

generation_summaries.description: The JZX90 and JZX100 Chaser and Mark II are the definitive Japanese drift sedans. The 1JZ-GTE twin-turbo inline-six produces 280bhp in stock form and is endlessly tunable. Four-door practicality, rear-wheel drive, and near-infinite power potential. Tourer V is the top spec.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Tourer V, Tourer S, Avante, Grande

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Tourer V, Tourer S, Avante, Grande

generation_summaries.description: The Altezza RS200 with the 3S-GE BEAMS engine is the driver's choice — 210bhp, six-speed manual, limited-slip differential. Sold in export markets as the Lexus IS200/IS300. The altezza tail-lights became a 2000s automotive fashion disaster but the car underneath is genuinely good.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS200, AS200, Lexus IS200, Lexus IS300

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: RS200, AS200, Lexus IS200, Lexus IS300

generation_summaries.description: The 510 Bluebird is Nissan's most significant early road car — the 'Poor Man's BMW 2002' that dominated SCCA sedan racing in America. Rear-wheel drive, independent rear suspension, and twin-cam options made it a genuine sports saloon. Now a cult car in the drift and classic JDM communities.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1400 Deluxe, 1600 SSS, 2-door, 4-door, Wagon

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1400 Deluxe, 1600 SSS, 2-door, 4-door, Wagon

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.8 L L28E I6,2.8 L L28ET Turbo I6
generation_summaries.description: The S130 280ZX was a significant commercial success but a departure from the S30's purity. More luxurious, heavier, but the Turbo model offered genuine performance. The 2+2 is the practical choice; the 2-seater Turbo the enthusiast pick. Values rising as S30 prices become prohibitive.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 280ZX, 280ZX Turbo, 280ZX 2+2, 10th Anniversary

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 280ZX, 280ZX Turbo, 280ZX 2+2, 10th Anniversary

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.8 L CA18DET Turbo I4,2.0 L SR20DET Turbo I4
generation_summaries.description: The S13 Silvia is the foundation of Japanese drift culture. Lightweight, rear-wheel drive, and with the SR20DET engine producing 205bhp in stock form — endlessly tunable to 500bhp+. The 180SX hatchback sibling shares the platform. The 240SX in North America used the same body with different engine.
generation_summaries.key_variants: K's, Q's, J's, 180SX, 240SX

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L SR20DE I4,2.0 L SR20DET Turbo I4
generation_summaries.description: The S14 grew the Silvia into a more complete package — wider track, better aero, and refined SR20DET. The NISMO-tuned 270RS and Autech versions are the collector targets. The Kouki (late) facelifted front end is more aggressive. Still the benchmark affordable RWD drift platform.
generation_summaries.key_variants: K's, Q's, NISMO 270RS, Autech, Kouki, Zenki

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L SR20DE I4,2.0 L SR20DET Turbo I4
generation_summaries.description: The S15 was the final Silvia and never officially sold in North America — making it the most desirable for US collectors under the 25-year import rule. Sharper styling, improved suspension, and optional six-speed Getrag gearbox. The Spec-R Aero with 250bhp is the ultimate S15.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Spec-R, Spec-S, Varietta Convertible, Autech

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: K's, Q's, J's, 180SX, 240SX, NISMO 270RS, Autech, Kouki, Zenki, Spec-R

generation_summaries.description: The R35 GT-R shocked the automotive world in 2007 — a production car lapping the Nürburgring in 7:29, outrunning cars costing twice the price. The dual-clutch transmission launches it to 60mph in 2.7 seconds. Nismo and Track Edition variants are the collector targets. Brutally quick, endlessly tuneable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Premium, Black Edition, Track Edition, Nismo, 45th Anniversary, 50th Anniversary

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Premium, Black Edition, Track Edition, Nismo, 45th Anniversary, 50th Anniversary

generation_summaries.engine_options: 3.5 L VQ35DE V6,3.5 L VQ35HR V6
generation_summaries.description: The 350Z revived the Z-car formula after the 300ZX was discontinued — rear-wheel drive, V6, affordable, and properly sporting. The Track and NISMO variants are the performance picks. The Roadster is the open-air choice. Now entering the zone where clean examples attract serious collectors.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Base, Touring, Track, NISMO, Roadster, 35th Anniversary

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Base, Touring, Track, NISMO, Roadster, 35th Anniversary

generation_summaries.description: The 370Z refined the 350Z with a shorter wheelbase, more power, and SynchroRev Match for perfect heel-and-toe downshifts. The NISMO variant with 350bhp and Rays wheels is the collector pick. The last of the classic Z-car lineage before the Z (RZ34).
generation_summaries.key_variants: Base, Touring, Sport, NISMO, Roadster

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Base, Touring, Sport, NISMO, Roadster

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.5 L RB25DET Turbo I6,2.5 L RB26DETT Twin-Turbo I6
generation_summaries.description: The Stagea WC34 Autech 260RS is the ultimate Q-car — a practical five-door estate with the complete GT-R drivetrain including the twin-turbo RB26DETT and ATTESA E-TS all-wheel drive. Just 1,000 260RS cars were built. Grocery runs at 150mph have never been more subtle.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS-Four, RS-X, Autech 260RS, 350RX

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: RS-Four, RS-X, Autech 260RS, 350RX

generation_summaries.description: The Silver Ghost earned its name from its near-silent running and silver paintwork — the original 40/50hp was the first car called 'the best car in the world' by the motoring press. Coachbuilt on a bare chassis, no two are identical. The 1907 London-to-Edinburgh trial proved its reliability. Among the most coveted veteran cars at auction.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 40/50hp, Alpine Eagle, London-Edinburgh

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 40/50hp, Alpine Eagle, London-Edinburgh

generation_summaries.description: The Phantom I succeeded the Silver Ghost with a new overhead-valve engine and central gearchange. Coachbuilt bodies by the finest coachbuilders — Barker, Hooper, Park Ward, Brewster in America. Lawrence of Arabia owned one. Every surviving example is individually documented.
generation_summaries.key_variants: New Phantom, Springfield Phantom

generation_summaries.description: The Phantom II introduced a new low-slung chassis that enabled more dramatic coachwork. The Continental version with short wheelbase and sporting body is the most desirable. Maharajas and royalty were the primary clientele. Barker and Gurney Nutting bodies are the most sought-after.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Continental, Limousine

generation_summaries.description: The Phantom III was the first Rolls-Royce V12 and the last pre-war Phantom. Independent front suspension was a technical landmark. Only 727 were completed before the war halted production. Each body was unique — Gurney Nutting, Windovers, and H.J. Mulliner produced the finest examples.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Sedanca de Ville

generation_summaries.description: The seventh-generation Phantom re-established Rolls-Royce as the world's pre-eminent luxury car under BMW ownership. Spaceframe aluminium construction, a 460bhp V12, and a rear-hinged coach door. The Drophead Coupe and Coupe variants are particularly collectible. Bespoke commissions through the Rolls-Royce Private Office command extraordinary premiums.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Phantom VII, Phantom EWB, Drophead Coupe, Coupe

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: New Phantom, Springfield Phantom, Standard, Continental, Limousine, Sedanca de Ville, Phantom VII, Phantom EWB, Drophead Coupe, Coupe

generation_summaries.description: The Silver Wraith was the first post-war Rolls-Royce, sold as a bare chassis for coachbuilding until 1955. Park Ward, H.J. Mulliner, and James Young produced the finest bodies. Long Wheelbase versions are the stateliest. The last Rolls-Royce sold exclusively as a chassis for coachwork.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard Wheelbase, Long Wheelbase

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard Wheelbase, Long Wheelbase

generation_summaries.description: The Silver Cloud is the definitive post-war Rolls-Royce shape — Rolls's first standard steel body designed in-house. The Silver Cloud II introduced the 6.2-litre V8; the III added quad headlamps. Convertible versions by Park Ward are among the most beautiful post-war British cars. The James Young two-door is exceptionally rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Silver Cloud I, Silver Cloud II, Silver Cloud III, Drophead Coupe, James Young Coupe

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Silver Cloud I, Silver Cloud II, Silver Cloud III, Drophead Coupe, James Young Coupe

generation_summaries.description: The Silver Shadow was the most radical Rolls-Royce in decades — unibody construction, four-wheel disc brakes, independent rear suspension. The most common Rolls-Royce ever made, which suppressed values for years. Now rising as condition examples become scarce. Two-door drophead coupe is the most desirable body style.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Silver Shadow I, Silver Shadow II, Two-door Saloon, Drophead Coupe, Long Wheelbase

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Silver Shadow I, Silver Shadow II, Two-door Saloon, Drophead Coupe, Long Wheelbase

generation_summaries.description: The Corniche convertible is the most glamorous post-war Rolls-Royce — and one of the longest-running models in automotive history at 24 years. Built by Mulliner Park Ward on the Silver Shadow platform. The Corniche S and final Series V with fuel injection are the most sophisticated. A Riviera staple.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Corniche, Corniche II, Corniche III, Corniche IV, Corniche S

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Corniche, Corniche II, Corniche III, Corniche IV, Corniche S

generation_summaries.description: The Silver Spirit updated the Silver Shadow's platform with contemporary styling, improved air conditioning, and from 1991 an electronic self-levelling suspension. The long-wheelbase Silver Spur is the chauffeur choice. The Silver Spirit III and Touring Limousine are the final refinements before the Silver Seraph.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Silver Spirit, Silver Spirit II, Silver Spirit III, Silver Spur, Touring Limousine

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Silver Spirit, Silver Spirit II, Silver Spirit III, Silver Spur, Touring Limousine

generation_summaries.description: The Silver Seraph was the first BMW-era Rolls-Royce — its 5.4-litre V12 was sourced from BMW's 750iL. The handbuilt body retained the traditional upright grille and classic proportions. Just 2,138 were made before the all-new Phantom arrived. The transition car between old and new Rolls-Royce.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Park Ward

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Park Ward

generation_summaries.description: The Lincoln Model K was America's finest coachbuilt car of the 1930s — a V12-powered platform bodied by Brunn, Judkins, LeBaron, and Willoughby into some of the most dramatic American automobiles ever made. Franklin D. Roosevelt's parade car was a Model K. The KB with the 7.0-litre V12 is the ultimate expression.
generation_summaries.key_variants: KA, KB, Judkins Coupe, LeBaron Convertible, Brunn Cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: KA, KB, Judkins Coupe, LeBaron Convertible, Brunn Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The 1940 Lincoln Continental is considered by many automotive historians the most beautiful American car ever designed. Edsel Ford sketched it himself as a personal car while vacationing in Florida. The cabriolet with its razor-edge styling, continental spare tyre, and low roofline set a standard that influenced decades of American car design.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Cabriolet, Club Coupe

generation_summaries.description: The Continental Mark II was America's most expensive production car when launched at $10,000 — nearly twice the price of a Cadillac Eldorado. Each was hand-built to order over 14 days on its own assembly line. Rust-proofed, individually matched panels, and personally inspected by company executives. A near-perfect American luxury coupe.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The 1961 Lincoln Continental is the most significant American car of the 1960s — four-door convertible with rear-hinged suicide doors, pure rectangular lines, and no unnecessary ornamentation. Elwood Engel designed it while at Chrysler; it won the IDSA Industrial Design Award. JFK rode in a stretched version in Dallas on November 22, 1963.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Sedan, Convertible, Executive Limousine

generation_summaries.description: The Mark III was Lincoln's answer to the Ford Thunderbird personal luxury coupe. Its neo-classic styling with fake spare tyre hump proved enormously popular. The Mark IV and V followed with growing dimensions. Elvis Presley famously owned multiple examples. The Mark V Bill Blass Edition is the most collectible.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mark III, Mark IV, Mark V, Bill Blass Edition, Cartier Edition, Pucci Edition

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Cabriolet, Club Coupe, Standard, Sedan, Convertible, Executive Limousine, Mark III, Mark IV, Mark V, Bill Blass Edition

generation_summaries.description: The Cosmopolitan was Lincoln's post-war statement of intent — a full-size luxury car competing directly with Cadillac. The convertible is extraordinarily rare. Lincoln finished second through fifth at the 1950 Pan-American Road Race with Cosmopolitans, establishing the nameplate's performance credibility.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Cosmopolitan, Custom

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Cosmopolitan, Custom

generation_summaries.description: The Capri and its successor Premiere represented Lincoln at its most elegant in the classic American era. The 1956-57 Premiere Convertible is one of the most handsome American open cars. Lincoln swept the top four positions in the 1952 Pan-American Road Race with production Capris.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Capri, Capri Convertible, Premiere, Premiere Convertible

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Capri, Capri Convertible, Premiere, Premiere Convertible

generation_summaries.engine_options: 5.0 L V8,4.6 L V8,4.6 L V8 SOHC
generation_summaries.description: The Town Car was Lincoln's mainstream flagship for three decades — the default American limousine base car, black-car staple, and retirement community favourite. The 1998–2002 Cartier Edition is the most complete; the final 2011 cars the most refined. Now rising as a long-wheelbase American classic of the late 20th century.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Signature, Cartier, Executive, Designer Series, Limousine

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Signature, Cartier, Executive, Designer Series, Limousine

generation_summaries.description: The Mark VIII is the last great Lincoln coupe — a sleek, aluminium-intensive body over an air-ride suspension and a 280bhp 4.6-litre DOHC V8. The 1997-98 LSC in black or white are the collector targets. Dramatically undervalued relative to its engineering and styling achievement.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, LSC

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, LSC

generation_summaries.description: The first Navigator created the American luxury SUV segment when it launched in 1997 and outsold the Cadillac Escalade for years. The 2003 Blackwood pickup variant is exceptionally rare. Early examples are now entering collector interest as defining artefacts of late 1990s American culture.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, Blackwood

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, Blackwood

generation_summaries.description: The 600 Grosser was the most technically ambitious car in the world when launched — a hydraulically operated everything: windows, seats, sunroof, boot lid, doors. At 5.5 metres and nearly 2.5 tonnes, it was the choice of heads of state, royalty, and dictators. Elvis, Coco Chanel, John Lennon, and Mao Zedong all owned one. The Landaulet is the rarest and most desirable body style.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Pullman, Landaulet, Short Wheelbase

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Pullman, Landaulet, Short Wheelbase

generation_summaries.description: The R107 SL is the longest-running Mercedes model in history at 18 years. Sold as the 350SL through to the 560SL, it is the definitive open Mercedes grand tourer. The 560SL is the most powerful and the American collector favourite. Hardtop and soft top supplied as standard on all cars.

The final 560SL of 1986-89 is the most powerful R107 and the most desirable for daily use. American-market cars with the full emissions package run reliably for decades. European-spec cars with the higher compression are scarcer and more sought after.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 560SL, 560SL roadster

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 350SL, 380SL, 450SL, 500SL, 560SL, 380SLC, 450SLC, 560SL roadster

generation_summaries.description: The W108 and long-wheelbase W109 are the S-Class that established Mercedes flagship supremacy. The 300SEL 6.3 — stuffed with the 600's V8 — was the fastest four-door sedan in the world in 1968. A German muscle car in a suit. The 300SEL 6.3 is the collector target; standard 280SE the accessible entry.

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.3 L Cosworth I4,2.5 L Cosworth I4
generation_summaries.description: The 190E 2.3-16 was developed with Cosworth — a 16-valve cylinder head on Mercedes' small sedan. Launched with a race at the Nürburgring where Ayrton Senna beat Niki Lauda. The Evolution I and Evolution II are homologation specials for DTM racing, with just 502 and 500 built respectively. The Evo II with its dramatic rear wing is the most desirable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 2.3-16, 2.5-16, Evolution I, Evolution II

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 2.3-16, 2.5-16, Evolution I, Evolution II

generation_summaries.description: The W124 Coupe is the finest everyday Mercedes ever made — understated, beautifully built, and with the optional 3.6-litre AMG engine, genuinely fast. The 300CE-24 with 24-valve head and the E36 AMG (3.6-litre) are the collector picks. The Cabriolet is the most elegant open Mercedes of the era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 300CE, 300CE-24, E320, E36 AMG, Cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 300CE, 300CE-24, E320, E36 AMG, Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The R129 SL introduced automatic rollbar deployment and was engineered to survive a rollover with the roof down. The 600SL with V12 is the ultimate; the 73 AMG with a 7.3-litre V12 and 525bhp is the most extreme. The SL60 AMG and SL55 AMG (later) are the performance picks for usability.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 300SL, 500SL, 600SL, SL60 AMG, SL73 AMG, 300SL, 500SL, 600SL

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 300SL, 500SL, 600SL, SL60 AMG, SL73 AMG

generation_summaries.description: The CLK GTR was built purely to homologate Mercedes for the FIA GT Championship — just 25 road cars and 1 roadster were required. Its 6.9-litre V12 produces 604bhp. The road car was almost identical to the race car. At $1.5 million new, it was the most expensive production car of its era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: CLK GTR, CLK GTR Roadster, CLK LM

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: CLK GTR, CLK GTR Roadster, CLK LM

generation_summaries.description: The SLS AMG was Mercedes AMG's first complete car — designed, engineered, and built entirely by AMG. Gullwing doors, a front-mid 6.2-litre naturally aspirated V8, and an aluminium spaceframe. The Electric Drive and Black Series are the extremes. The last naturally aspirated AMG flagship.
generation_summaries.key_variants: SLS AMG, SLS AMG Roadster, SLS AMG GT, SLS AMG Black Series, SLS AMG Electric Drive, SLS AMG, SLS AMG GT, SLS AMG Black Series

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: SLS AMG, SLS AMG Roadster, SLS AMG GT, SLS AMG Black Series, SLS AMG Electric Drive, SLS AMG GT Final Edition, SLS Electric Drive

generation_summaries.description: AMG took the W124 sedan and fitted a 6.0-litre V8 producing 381bhp — a Q-car of devastating effectiveness. Built in tiny numbers by AMG before their official Mercedes partnership. The E60 AMG and its companion the E36 AMG represent the last of the old-school AMG tuner era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: E60 AMG, E36 AMG

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: E60 AMG, E36 AMG

generation_summaries.description: The E9 coupe is one of the most beautiful BMW road cars ever made. The CSL — Coupe Sport Leichtbau — stripped weight with aluminium panels and thin glass. The Batmobile CSL with full aero kit dominated European Touring Car racing 1973–1975. Road-spec CSLs with the aero package are extraordinarily collectible.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 2500CS, 2800CS, 3.0CS, 3.0CSi, 3.0CSL, Batmobile, 2800CS, 3.0CS

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 2500CS, 2800CS, 3.0CS, 3.0CSi, 3.0CSL, Batmobile

generation_summaries.description: The E24 6 Series is the grand touring BMW — elegant Karmann coachwork over the 5 Series platform. The M635 CSi shares the M1's engine and is the driver's pick; the 635CSi the gentleman's express. US-market L6 and M6 variants use the same codes but detuned engines.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 628CSi, 630CS, 633CSi, 635CSi, M635 CSi, M6 (US), 630CS, 633CSi

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 628CSi, 630CS, 633CSi, 635CSi, M635 CSi, M6 (US), M635CSi, L6

generation_summaries.description: The E34 M5 refined the E28's concept with a larger engine, better ergonomics, and the option of a Touring estate — the only M5 Touring ever made. The 3.8-litre later cars are the most powerful; the Touring is the rarest and most desirable M5 variant ever built. Just 891 Tourings were made.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Sedan 3.5, Sedan 3.8, Touring

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Sedan 3.5, Sedan 3.8, Touring

generation_summaries.description: The E36 M3 is the most underrated BMW M car. Dismissed between the celebrated E30 and E46, it is now recognised as a supremely capable grand touring sports car. European-spec S50 engine is superior to the US S52. The Lightweight (M3/4/5) is the American homologation special. Convertibles are usable classics.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Coupe, Sedan, Convertible, Lightweight M3/4/5, GT

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Coupe, Sedan, Convertible, Lightweight M3/4/5, GT

generation_summaries.description: The E39 M5 is widely considered the greatest everyday performance saloon ever made. The S62 V8 produces 394bhp and revs to 7,000rpm with a sound unlike any other road car. Manual gearbox only. The car that cemented the M5 as the benchmark by which all performance saloons are judged.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The Z8 was Chris Bangle's homage to the 507 — a hand-built roadster with the E39 M5's V8 and retro-modern styling by Henrik Fisker. Only 5,703 were made. James Bond drove one in The World Is Not Enough. The Alpina Roadster V8 is a limited edition variant. Values have risen steadily for a decade.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Z8, Alpina Roadster V8

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Z8, Alpina Roadster V8

generation_summaries.description: The M Roadster and M Coupe used the Z3 body with the M3's drivetrain — the Coupe particularly became known as the 'clown shoe' for its unusual roofline. The S54-engined final cars are the most powerful and most valuable. The M Coupe is now one of the most collectable modern BMWs.
generation_summaries.key_variants: M Roadster S52, M Roadster S54, M Coupe S52, M Coupe S54

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: M Roadster S52, M Roadster S54, M Coupe S52, M Coupe S54

generation_summaries.description: The Ur-Quattro is one of the most consequential cars of the 20th century -- it proved that four-wheel drive could make a car faster rather than heavier, and it changed rallying forever. The early 10-valve cars are the purest; matching-numbers, well-documented examples are genuine collector pieces.
generation_summaries.key_variants: WR, WX, MB, RR, 10V turbo

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.1 L Turbo I5,2.2 L Turbo I5
generation_summaries.description: The Ur-Quattro (original Quattro) transformed rallying overnight — four-wheel drive in a production-based car was unbeatable on loose surfaces. Hannu Mikkola and Michèle Mouton dominated WRC in 1982–84. The road car introduced permanent AWD to production cars. The 20V variant with 220bhp is the final and finest. One of the most significant cars of the 20th century.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Quattro 10V, Quattro 20V, WR (Werkswagen), 20V, 20V turbo, RR, 1989, 1990

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Quattro 10V, Quattro 20V, WR (Werkswagen), 20V, 20V turbo, RR, 1989, 1990, 1991, WR

generation_summaries.description: The Sport Quattro was built for Group B rally homologation — just 200 road cars required. Shorter wheelbase than the Ur-Quattro, wider arches, 306bhp, and a kerb weight under 1,300kg. Stig Blomqvist won the 1984 WRC drivers title in it. The road car cost more than a Ferrari at launch. One of the most collectible German cars.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard, S1 Evolution

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard, S1 Evolution

generation_summaries.description: The RS2 Avant was developed jointly with Porsche — Porsche fitted the brakes, wheels, mirrors, and door handles from the 911, while Audi contributed the 315bhp turbocharged five-cylinder. The world's fastest estate car in 1994. Every RS2 had a Porsche badge on the brake callipers. The car that defined the fast estate genre.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS2 Avant

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: RS2 Avant

generation_summaries.description: The original TT is one of the most beautiful cars of the 1990s — Bauhaus design language applied to a performance coupe. Early 225bhp quattro cars suffered handling problems that led to a controversial recall and rear spoiler addition. The 3.2 VR6 with DSG is the definitive variant. The Roadster is the open-air collector pick.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1.8T, 1.8T quattro, 3.2 VR6, Roadster, TT Sport

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1.8T, 1.8T quattro, 3.2 VR6, Roadster, TT Sport

generation_summaries.description: The Audi S1 E2 was the ultimate evolution of Group B — a five-cylinder producing over 500bhp with twin sequential turbos, four-wheel drive, and a 0-60mph time under 3 seconds. Walter Rohrl and Michele Mouton drove it. The road cars (if any exist) are effectively priceless competition vehicles.
generation_summaries.key_variants: E1, E2, S1 Pikes Peak

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: E1, E2, S1 Pikes Peak

generation_summaries.description: The R8 was Audi's first mid-engine supercar and transformed the brand's performance image overnight. Derived from the Le Mans-winning R8 race car, it introduced the V10 engine later adopted by Lamborghini Huracan. The V10 Plus is the collector target; the Spyder the open-air choice. Iron Man drove one.
generation_summaries.key_variants: R8 V8, R8 V10, R8 V10 Plus, R8 Spyder V8, R8 Spyder V10, GT, 4.2 V8, 5.2 V10

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: R8 V8, R8 V10, R8 V10 Plus, R8 Spyder V8, R8 Spyder V10, GT, 4.2 V8, 5.2 V10, R8 GT, R8 LMS

generation_summaries.description: The 100 Coupe S was Audi's first significant sporting coupe — a graceful fastback design that previewed the brand's ambitions. Powered by a 1.8-litre engine with 115bhp, it was quick for its era. Increasingly recognised as a design masterpiece and a future classic of 1970s German styling.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Standard

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Standard

generation_summaries.description: The Scirocco was Giorgetto Giugiaro's masterpiece on the Golf platform — a sporting coupe of genuine beauty. The Mk1 is the purist's car; the Mk2 the more refined. The 16V and GTX Scala are the performance variants. Increasingly collectable as unmodified examples become rare.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Mk1 TS, Mk1 GLi, Mk2 GTX, Mk2 16V, Mk2 Scala

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Mk1 TS, Mk1 GLi, Mk2 GTX, Mk2 16V, Mk2 Scala

generation_summaries.engine_options: 1.8 L G60 I4,2.0 L 16V I4,2.9 L VR6,2.0 L Turbo I4
generation_summaries.description: The Corrado was Volkswagen's flagship coupe — wider, heavier, and more powerful than the Scirocco it replaced. The G60 supercharged model was quick for its era; the VR6 with its narrow-angle six-cylinder is the collector target. The active rear spoiler was a first for a production car at its price point. Increasingly undervalued.
generation_summaries.key_variants: G60, 16V, VR6, Storm

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: G60, 16V, VR6, Storm

generation_summaries.description: The Mk4 R32 was the first Golf with four-wheel drive and a VR6 engine producing 241bhp. DSG dual-clutch gearbox only (no manual). Brutally quick for a Golf, with a distinctive VR6 exhaust note. The launch car for both the R32 nameplate and DSG transmission. Low-mileage examples are becoming collectible.

The Phaeton was Ferdinand Piëch's personal mission — to prove Volkswagen could build a car superior to Mercedes S-Class and BMW 7 Series. The W12 and V10 TDI are the powertrain stories. Hand-built in the Glass Manufaktur in Dresden. A commercial failure but an engineering triumph. Deeply undervalued.
generation_summaries.key_variants: V6, V8, W12, V10 TDI, Long Wheelbase

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: V6, V8, W12, V10 TDI, Long Wheelbase

generation_summaries.description: The original Monte Carlo was Chevrolet's personal luxury answer to the Pontiac Grand Prix. The SS 454 -- available only in 1970 -- is the blue-chip collector piece: low production, biggest engine, handsome proportions.
generation_summaries.key_variants: base, SS, SS 454

generation_summaries.description: SS models with the 454 in 1973 bridge muscle and personal luxury, representing solid and undervalued collector territory.
generation_summaries.key_variants: base, S, Landau, SS, 454 SS

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: base, SS, SS 454, S, Landau, 454 SS

generation_summaries.description: The 1969 Torino Talladega -- a slippery fastback built for NASCAR homologation in fewer than 750 units -- is the ultimate Torino collector piece. The Cobra with the 428 Cobra Jet is the street-performance pinnacle.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Cobra, Talladega, GT, Fairlane Cobra, 428 CJ

generation_summaries.description: The Starsky & Hutch Gran Torino became a pop-culture icon. The 1971 Cobra with the 429 CJ is the pure performance pick; 1972 is the last year of real grunt before emissions choked output.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Sport, Cobra, Squire Wagon, Brougham, Gran Torino, Gran Torino Sport, Gran Torino Squire

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Cobra, Talladega, GT, Fairlane Cobra, 428 CJ, Sport, Squire Wagon, Brougham, Gran Torino, Gran Torino Sport

generation_summaries.description: The compact Dart GTS with the 340 four-barrel is the lightweight sleeper of the Mopar world. Hemi Darts, built in tiny numbers, are the most extreme and valuable.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GTS, Swinger, Swinger 340, Sport, 340, 383 Hemi, Hemi, GT convertible

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GTS, Swinger, Swinger 340, Sport, 340, 383 Hemi, Hemi, GT convertible

generation_summaries.engine_options: 6.3 L 383 Magnum,7.0 L 426 Hemi,7.2 L 440 Six Pack
generation_summaries.description: The Super Bee stripped the Coronet to essentials and stuffed in the 383 Magnum as standard. The 440 Six Pack cars are the most collectible; the 1969 cars with the bumblebee stripe are defining images of the muscle era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 383 Magnum, 440, 440 Six Pack, Hemi, A-833 4-speed

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 383 Magnum, 440, 440 Six Pack, Hemi, A-833 4-speed

generation_summaries.description: The Demon was Dodge's compact performance answer with the optional 340 three-two-barrel. The 1971 Demon 340 in GSS trim is among the most complete factory performance packages of the era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 340, 340 Three-Two, 318, Sizzler

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 340, 340 Three-Two, 318, Sizzler

generation_summaries.description: The GTX came standard with the 440 Super Commando -- an engine most rivals offered only as a costly option. Hemi convertibles are among the most valuable Mopar collectibles; just 17 were built in 1971.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 440, Hemi, convertible, hardtop

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 440, Hemi, convertible, hardtop

generation_summaries.description: The 1970-71 'Cuda is the most collectible Plymouth muscle car. Hemi 'Cuda convertibles consistently set records at auction. The AAR 'Cuda, built for SCCA Trans-Am homologation, is a rare race-bred variant.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 'Cuda 340, 'Cuda 383, 'Cuda 440, Hemi 'Cuda, AAR 'Cuda, 'Cuda convertible

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 'Cuda 340, 'Cuda 383, 'Cuda 440, Hemi 'Cuda, AAR 'Cuda, 'Cuda convertible

generation_summaries.description: The Super Duty 455 Trans Am is widely regarded as the greatest muscle car of the emissions era -- 310 net hp at a time when competitors struggled to make 200. One of the most important Pontiacs ever built.
generation_summaries.key_variants: SD-455 Coupe, SD-455 Formula

generation_summaries.description: Smokey and the Bandit made the black-and-gold Trans Am the most desired car in America for a generation. The 1978 Special Edition with T-tops and screaming chicken hood decal is a time-capsule collectible.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Special Edition, base, T/A 6.6, 403

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: SD-455 Coupe, SD-455 Formula, Special Edition, base, T/A 6.6, 403

generation_summaries.engine_options: 6.6 L 400,7.5 L 455,6.6 L Ram Air III
generation_summaries.description: The 1969 Grand Prix SJ is one of the most stylish American cars of its era -- long hood, short deck. The 455 HO cars are the performance pick and remain surprisingly undervalued.
generation_summaries.key_variants: SJ, 455 HO, Ram Air III, base

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: SJ, 455 HO, Ram Air III, base

generation_summaries.description: The Cutlass W-31 with force-air induction 350 is an overlooked lightweight; the Hurst/Olds collaboration produced some of the most striking factory muscle cars of 1968-69.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 442, W-31, W-30, Supreme, Rallye 350, Cutlass S

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 442, W-31, W-30, Supreme, Rallye 350, Cutlass S

generation_summaries.description: The original 1968 Hurst/Olds was assembled by Hurst off-site to bypass GM's engine displacement rules. Just 515 were built, making the original the most valuable. The 1969 cars in gold and white are instantly recognized.

The Buick GSX Stage 1 is the most underrated muscle car of 1970. Its 455 produced more torque than any American production engine of the era -- 510 lb-ft. Saturn Yellow and Apollo White are the signature colors.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Stage 1, Stage 1 4-speed, Stage 1 automatic

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Stage 1, Stage 1 4-speed, Stage 1 automatic

generation_summaries.description: The Skylark Gran Sport predates the GTO in concept. The 1969 GS 400 Stage 1 convertible is the definitive version: big-displacement torque in an elegant body.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GS 340, GS 400, GS 400 Stage 1, GS California, convertible

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GS 340, GS 400, GS 400 Stage 1, GS California, convertible

generation_summaries.description: The Rebel Machine was AMC's most extroverted muscle statement: factory red-white-blue livery with a functional scoop and 340 hp. Just 2,326 built in 1970.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 390 V8, auto, 4-speed

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 390 V8, auto, 4-speed

generation_summaries.description: Built with Hurst in just 1,512 units, the SC/Rambler is one of the wildest factory sleepers of the muscle era. Stuffed with the 390 and wearing Hurst livery, it ran mid-14-second quarters from the factory.
generation_summaries.key_variants: A package, B package, C package

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: A package, B package, C package

generation_summaries.description: The 1965 Shelby GT350 -- built in Carroll Shelby's LAX shop from plain white Mustang fastbacks -- is the foundation of American performance. The R-model racing variant is one of the most historically significant American race cars. The 1965-66 cars are the most original and collectible.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT350, GT350R, GT350H (Hertz), GT350 convertible, 1965 original, 1966, 1967, 1968

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GT350, GT350R, GT350H (Hertz), GT350 convertible, 1965 original, 1966, 1967, 1968, 1969, 1970

generation_summaries.description: The GT500 brought a big-block to the Shelby formula. The KR (King of the Road) 428 Cobra Jet of 1968 is the mechanical high point. The 1967 fastback is the most recognized Shelby silhouette worldwide.
generation_summaries.key_variants: GT500, GT500KR, GT500 convertible, Eleanor

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: GT500, GT500KR, GT500 convertible, Eleanor

generation_summaries.description: The Cadillac DeVille convertible of the 1960s represents American optimism at its peak. The 1964 with its clean pre-fin body and standard 429 is the most resolved design. Final 1970 convertibles are high-demand last-of-a-kind pieces.
generation_summaries.key_variants: DeVille, DeVille Convertible, Fleetwood DeVille, Hardtop, Park Avenue

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: DeVille, DeVille Convertible, Fleetwood DeVille, Hardtop, Park Avenue

generation_summaries.description: The Studebaker Golden Hawk was America's first factory supercharged car -- the 1957-58 models used a Paxton blower on the 289 to produce 275 hp. An engineering milestone from an independent automaker, and deeply undervalued at auction.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 1956 Packard V8, 1957 Supercharged, 1958 Supercharged

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 1956 Packard V8, 1957 Supercharged, 1958 Supercharged

generation_summaries.description: The Maverick Grabber with the 302 is a lightweight compact muscle sleeper and one of the best-value collector Fords. The rare 1970-71 cars with 3-speed manual and Grabber stripes are the ones to find.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Grabber, 302 V8, Sprint, Luxury Decor, base

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Grabber, 302 V8, Sprint, Luxury Decor, base

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.7 L Flat-6,3.4 L S,3.4 L R,3.8 L GT4 proto
generation_summaries.description: The 987 Cayman is structurally the most rigid Porsche of its era -- a mid-engine coupe that many engineers considered potentially faster than the 911 before Porsche intervened on power output. The Cayman R with weight reduction and 330 hp is the collector variant.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Cayman, Cayman S, Cayman R

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Cayman, Cayman S, Cayman R

generation_summaries.description: The W111 cabriolet is among the most beautiful postwar Mercedes-Benz bodies. Fewer than 6,000 were built across all variants; the 280SE 3.5 V8 cabriolet is the ultimate specification. These are genuinely rare cars that command serious auction premiums when presented in original condition.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 220SE coupe, 250SE coupe, 280SE coupe, 220SE cabriolet, 250SE cabriolet, 280SE cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 220SE coupe, 250SE coupe, 280SE coupe, 220SE cabriolet, 250SE cabriolet, 280SE cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The 280SE 3.5 cabriolet is one of the most coveted postwar European cars -- a hand-built open Mercedes with a V8, produced for just two years in tiny numbers. Values have escalated dramatically; concours examples regularly achieve seven figures.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 280SE 3.5 cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 280SE 3.5 cabriolet

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L I4,2.3 L I4,2.8 L I6,3.0 L diesel,5.0 L V8 AMG
generation_summaries.description: The W123 is the benchmark of Mercedes-Benz engineering -- overbuilt, endlessly reliable, and now increasingly collectible. The 230E coupe is the gentleman's choice; AMG-converted examples with the 5.0 V8 are rare sleepers. Diesels with documented high mileage have become a cult unto themselves.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 230E, 230CE coupe, 280E, 300D, 300TD wagon, 300D turbo, AMG 5.0

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 230E, 230CE coupe, 280E, 300D, 300TD wagon, 300D turbo, AMG 5.0

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.3 L I4,2.6 L I6,3.0 L I6,3.2 L I6,5.0 L V8 AMG,6.0 L AMG Hammer
generation_summaries.description: The W124 300E is widely regarded as the finest sedan Mercedes-Benz ever built. The AMG 6.0-litre Hammer conversion -- stuffing the 560SEL engine into the 300E body -- created one of the fastest sedans of the late 1980s. Wagons and cabriolets are the most collectible body styles.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 230E, 260E, 300E, 300CE coupe, 300TE wagon, E320, E500, AMG Hammer

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 230E, 260E, 300E, 300CE coupe, 300TE wagon, E320, E500, AMG Hammer, 320CE cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The W126 SEC coupe is arguably the most elegant German coupe of the 1980s. Bruno Sacco's design has aged beautifully. The 560SEC is the performance specification; AMG-converted examples with the 6.0 engine are the ultimate sleepers of the era.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 380SEC, 500SEC, 560SEC, AMG 6.0 SEC

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 380SEC, 500SEC, 560SEC, AMG 6.0 SEC

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.3 L I4,2.8 L I6,3.0 L diesel,5.0 L V8,5.5 L V8 AMG,6.0 L AMG
generation_summaries.description: The original G-Wagen is the most utilitarian vehicle to wear a three-pointed star, and its longevity -- essentially unchanged from 1979 to 2018 -- is a testament to its engineering. Early diesels in original condition are classic commercial-vehicle collectibles; AMG G55 and G63 6x6 editions represent excess taken to an absurd and wonderful extreme.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 230G, 300GD, G500, G55 AMG, G63 AMG, G63 6x6, G300 diesel

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 230G, 300GD, G500, G55 AMG, G63 AMG, G63 6x6, G300 diesel

generation_summaries.description: The AMG Hammer is one of the great automotive sleepers of all time -- a 300E body concealing a bored-out 6.0-litre V8 producing 375 hp, making it the fastest sedan in the world upon its debut. Fewer than 100 are believed to have been converted; the wagon version is among the most desirable AMG vehicles ever built.
generation_summaries.key_variants: Hammer sedan, Hammer wagon, 300E 6.0

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: Hammer sedan, Hammer wagon, 300E 6.0

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L I4,2.3 L Kompressor,3.2 L V6 AMG
generation_summaries.description: The SLK R170 introduced the folding metal hardtop to the roadster segment and was an instant hit. The AMG 32 with its supercharged V6 is the performance pick; the 230 Kompressor is the approachable entry point that is now genuinely affordable and mechanically simple.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 200 Kompressor, 230 Kompressor, 320, 32 AMG

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 200 Kompressor, 230 Kompressor, 320, 32 AMG

generation_summaries.description: The R230 SL returned to a proper two-seat roadster with an updated folding metal roof. The SL55 AMG with its supercharged 5.5 is the sweet spot -- sophisticated, fast, and now entering genuine classic territory. The SL65 with its 604 hp biturbo V12 is the ultimate excess specification.
generation_summaries.key_variants: SL500, SL55 AMG, SL600, SL65 AMG, SL350

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: SL500, SL55 AMG, SL600, SL65 AMG, SL350

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L I4,2.3 L Kompressor,3.2 L V6,4.3 L V8,5.5 L AMG
generation_summaries.description: The W208 CLK 55 AMG is an underrated performance coupe that combined elegant styling with serious performance. The cabriolet in CLK 430 or 55 AMG specification is a sophisticated open car that represents outstanding value today.
generation_summaries.key_variants: CLK200, CLK230 Kompressor, CLK320, CLK430, CLK55 AMG, cabriolet

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: CLK200, CLK230 Kompressor, CLK320, CLK430, CLK55 AMG, cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The E30 is the most beloved BMW of any generation -- a perfectly proportioned, rear-drive compact with communicative steering and a chassis that rewards the driver. The convertible in 325i specification is a clean, attainable classic; the M3 sits in its own category entirely.

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 316, 318i, 320i, 323i, 325i, 325e, 325iX, 325i convertible, 325i Touring, M3

generation_summaries.description: The E36 brought multi-link rear suspension and a more polished ride without sacrificing driver engagement. The M3 in coupe or convertible form is the collector piece; the 328i is the value sweet spot -- a genuinely sporting car at an attainable price.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 318i, 320i, 323i, 325i, 328i, 328i convertible, 328i Touring, M3

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 318i, 320i, 323i, 325i, 328i, 328i convertible, 328i Touring, M3, M3 GT

generation_summaries.description: The E28 525i and 528i are exemplars of 1980s BMW engineering at its most purposeful. The rare 533i and 535i offer real performance; the M5 derivative sits atop the range as the first genuine performance executive sedan.

The E34 Touring is the most desirable body style -- BMW's elegant station wagon with the 525i or 530i is the gentleman's load-lugger. The 540i with the V8 is a sophisticated long-distance machine. The M5 in Touring guise is among the most valuable production BMWs.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 520i, 525i, 530i, 535i, 540i, M5, 525i Touring, M5 Touring

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 520i, 525i, 530i, 535i, 540i, M5, 525i Touring, M5 Touring

generation_summaries.description: The E31 8 Series was the most technologically ambitious BMW of its era -- V12 power, fly-by-wire throttle, and an interior that still impresses. The 850CSi with the 375 hp S70 V12 is the performance pinnacle and one of the rarest production BMWs; only 1,510 were built.

The Z3 M Coupe is the "clown shoe" -- a shooting brake body on a roadster platform with a straight-six M engine. Dismissed at launch and now one of the most sought-after BMWs of the era. The S54-powered final cars are the ones to find.
generation_summaries.key_variants: M Roadster S50, M Roadster S52, M Roadster S54, M Coupe S52, M Coupe S54

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: M Roadster S50, M Roadster S52, M Roadster S54, M Coupe S52, M Coupe S54

generation_summaries.description: The Z4 M Roadster and M Coupe carry the S54 from the E46 M3 in a lighter, more focused package. The M Coupe especially is a rare and increasingly appreciated driver's car -- stiffer, sharper, and with a manual gearbox as standard.
generation_summaries.key_variants: M Roadster, M Coupe

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: M Roadster, M Coupe

generation_summaries.description: The 2002 tii is the most desirable road-going 2002 -- Kugelfischer mechanical fuel injection gave it the sharpest throttle response of any production 2002. These are now significant collector cars; unrestored, matching-numbers cars with documented history are especially prized.
generation_summaries.key_variants: tii, tii Touring, tii automatic

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: tii, tii Touring, tii automatic

generation_summaries.description: The Audi S2 Avant is the original performance wagon -- a turbocharged five-cylinder quattro machine that prefigured two decades of RS models. Low production numbers and age have made these increasingly rare; documented, rust-free examples are hard to find.
generation_summaries.key_variants: S2 Coupe, S2 Avant, S2 Cabriolet

generation_summaries.description: The RS2 Avant was developed with Porsche -- the brakes, wheels, and mirrors came directly from the 964. With 315 hp and a 0-100 km/h time that shamed contemporary supercars, it is the godfather of the RS line and one of the most desirable Audis ever made.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS2 Avant

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: S2 Coupe, S2 Avant, S2 Cabriolet, RS2 Avant

generation_summaries.description: The B5 S4 with its twin-turbocharged 2.7 biturbo is one of the great performance sleepers -- conservative styling that disguises serious pace. Stage 1 to 3 tuning potential from the biturbo platform is enormous; stock examples with low miles and documented service are the collector target.
generation_summaries.key_variants: S4 sedan, S4 Avant, S4 Avant Plus

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: S4 sedan, S4 Avant, S4 Avant Plus

generation_summaries.description: The C5 RS6 with Lamborghini-derived twin-turbocharged V8 is the definitive fast estate of the era. The Avant is the collector body style; saloons are rarer in the UK market. A well-maintained RS6 Avant is among the most practical collectibles in this guide.
generation_summaries.key_variants: RS6 sedan, RS6 Avant, RS6 Plus

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: RS6 sedan, RS6 Avant, RS6 Plus

generation_summaries.engine_options: 2.0 L TFSI,3.2 L VR6,2.5 L RS TT
generation_summaries.description: The 8J TT RS with its five-cylinder 2.5 TFSI is the collector variant -- one of the last Audis with the characterful inline-five, producing 340 hp in a taut coupe body. The TT RS Plus with 360 hp is the peak specification.
generation_summaries.key_variants: TT S, TT RS, TT RS Plus, 3.2 quattro, 2.0 TFSI, roadster

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: TT S, TT RS, TT RS Plus, 3.2 quattro, 2.0 TFSI, roadster

generation_summaries.engine_options: 5.2 L NA V10,5.2 L V10 Plus/Performance
generation_summaries.description: The second-gen R8 refined the naturally aspirated V10 formula with sharper steering and a more focused chassis. The V10 Performance in final form represents the last naturally aspirated supercar from Audi; the final RWD variants stripped back to rear-wheel drive are the driver's choice.
generation_summaries.key_variants: V10, V10 Plus, V10 Performance, V10 RWD, Spyder V10

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: V10, V10 Plus, V10 Performance, V10 RWD, Spyder V10

generation_summaries.description: The Audi V8 Quattro was the company's first proper luxury saloon and the first Audi with a V8. Its quattro drivetrain and understated styling made it a genuine alternative to the BMW 7 Series. The later 4.2 with the manual gearbox is the performance pick and the most collectible.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 3.6 V8, 4.2 V8, 4.2 manual, Typ 4C

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 3.6 V8, 4.2 V8, 4.2 manual, Typ 4C

generation_summaries.description: The 200 Quattro Turbo is the undersung hero of the Audi performance range -- the five-cylinder turbo in a full-size body with four-wheel drive. The Avant version especially is a rare and practical performance estate.
generation_summaries.key_variants: 200 Avant, 200 sedan, Typ 44

model_descriptions.variant_mentions: 200 Avant, 200 sedan, Typ 44

generation_summaries.description: The original XJ6 is widely considered one of the finest saloons ever made -- Lyons achieved a combination of ride, handling, refinement, and style at a price that humbled Rolls-Royce. The Series I in 4.2 form is the purist choice; the rare two-door coupe is one of the most beautiful Jaguar bodies.
generation_summaries.key_variants: XJ6 2.8, XJ6 4.2, XJ12, XJ coupe, Daimler Double Six

generation_summaries.description: The Pininfarina-facelifted Series III is the longest-running and most refined of the original XJ shape. The 1988-92 Sovereign and Vanden Plas with the 4.0 straight-six represent the mature expression of the design -- elegant, fast, and deeply undervalued today.
generation_summaries.key_variants: XJ6, XJ12, Sovereign, Vanden Plas, Daimler
